magnesium-pritchard.indication: Eclampsia: stop seizures and prevent recurrence
magnesium-pritchard.dose: 4 g IV loading, then 5 g deep IM into EACH buttock (10 g IM total); maintenance 5 g IM into alternate buttocks
magnesium-pritchard.duration: Continue until 24 hours after birth OR the last seizure, whichever is later
magnesium-pritchard.preparation: Using 50% (500 mg/mL): 4 g = 8 mL; dilute in 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9% and infuse over 15–20 min. Each 5 g IM dose = 10 mL of 50% solution. Check the actual ampoule strength.
magnesium-pritchard.maxDose: Do not give maintenance when toxicity criteria are present; do not run an additional magnesium regimen
monitoring: Check patellar reflexes, respiratory rate and hourly urine output; monitor BP, pulse and consciousness
Withhold magnesium for absent reflexes, respiratory rate <12/min or urine <100 mL in 4 h; obtain serum magnesium and senior review
Stop magnesium and support ventilation for toxicity; give the calcium-gluconate antidote shown below
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis, heart block or magnesium toxicity
Renal impairment or oliguria requires reduced/withheld maintenance and more frequent assessment

magnesium-iv.indication: Eclampsia: alternative when a reliable infusion pump and monitoring are available
magnesium-iv.dose: 4 g IV loading over 15–20 min, then 1 g/hour
magnesium-iv.frequency: One loading dose, then continuous infusion
magnesium-iv.duration: 24 hours after birth or last seizure, whichever is later
magnesium-iv.preparation: 50% solution: withdraw 8 mL (4 g) into 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9% for loading; for maintenance make 20 g up to a FINAL 100 mL (200 mg/mL), run at 5 mL/hour by labelled pump
magnesium-iv.maxDose: Use ONE IV or IV/IM protocol; stop/adjust for toxicity or renal dysfunction
monitoring: Check patellar reflexes, respiratory rate and hourly urine output; monitor BP, pulse and consciousness
Withhold magnesium for absent reflexes, respiratory rate <12/min or urine <100 mL in 4 h; obtain serum magnesium and senior review
Stop magnesium and support ventilation for toxicity; give the calcium-gluconate antidote shown below
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis, heart block or magnesium toxicity
Renal impairment or oliguria requires reduced/withheld maintenance and more frequent assessment
notes: Maintenance concentration and pump rate are calculated from the prescribed 1 g/hour; independently check the preparation.

magnesium-recurrence.indication: Recurrent eclamptic convulsion after loading; reassess airway, glucose and magnesium toxicity
magnesium-recurrence.dose: 2 g IV additional dose after senior assessment
magnesium-recurrence.frequency: One rescue dose, followed by reassessment
magnesium-recurrence.duration: Acute rescue; continue the selected maintenance regimen
magnesium-recurrence.preparation: 50% solution: 2 g = 4 mL, dilute in compatible sodium chloride 0.9%; give slowly by infusion and check the total loading already received
magnesium-recurrence.maxDose: MSF ceiling: no more than 8 g IV in the first hour; persistent fits need anaesthesia/ICU, not repeated blind magnesium dosing
monitoring: Check patellar reflexes, respiratory rate and hourly urine output; monitor BP, pulse and consciousness
Withhold magnesium for absent reflexes, respiratory rate <12/min or urine <100 mL in 4 h; obtain serum magnesium and senior review
Stop magnesium and support ventilation for toxicity; give the calcium-gluconate antidote shown below
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis, heart block or magnesium toxicity
Renal impairment or oliguria requires reduced/withheld maintenance and more frequent assessment

magnesium-neuro.indication: Imminent preterm birth: NICE offers at 24+0–29+6 weeks and considers at 30+0–33+6 weeks; discuss 23+0–23+6 individually
magnesium-neuro.duration: Stop at birth or 24 hours, whichever occurs first
magnesium-neuro.preparation: 50%: 4 g = 8 mL diluted in compatible sodium chloride 0.9%; maintenance example 20 g made up to FINAL 100 mL, 5 mL/hour via pump
magnesium-neuro.maxDose: 24 hours for neuroprotection; do not add to an eclampsia regimen already running
monitoring: Record pulse, BP, respiratory rate and tendon reflexes at least every 4 h; more often if oliguria or renal impairment
contraindications: Myasthenia gravis, heart block or magnesium toxicity
Renal impairment or oliguria requires reduced/withheld maintenance and more frequent assessment

calcium-magnesium-toxicity.indication: Antidote for clinically significant magnesium toxicity
calcium-magnesium-toxicity.frequency: Initial antidote dose; reassess breathing, ECG and calcium before further dosing
calcium-magnesium-toxicity.duration: Emergency reversal; stop magnesium and support the airway concurrently
calcium-magnesium-toxicity.preparation: 10% = 100 mg/mL; 10 mL contains 1 g calcium gluconate, NOT 1 g elemental calcium. Give over at least 5 min through a patent IV line; do not mix with other drugs
calcium-magnesium-toxicity.maxDose: No automatic repeated-dose course; further calcium requires monitored reassessment
monitoring: Continuous ECG/heart rate; respiratory status, reflexes and injection site; serum calcium/magnesium where available
contraindications: Extravasation can cause tissue injury; take special care with digoxin
Do not confuse calcium gluconate with calcium chloride

oxytocin-prevention.indication: Prevention of PPH after birth, distinct from treatment or labour augmentation
oxytocin-prevention.route: IM (or slow IV by the approved birth-unit protocol)
oxytocin-prevention.preparation: For a 10 IU/mL ampoule: 10 IU = 1 mL IM. Verify the strength. Never give a rapid undiluted IV bolus
monitoring: Quantified blood loss, uterine tone, BP/pulse, perfusion and urine output; record every dose and time
Persistent shock or bleeding needs source control and blood products in parallel; do not wait for all drug doses
contraindications: Do not use the PPH dose or infusion rate for labour induction

oxytocin-pph.indication: Atonic bleeding after delivery; treatment continues alongside the PPH bundle
oxytocin-pph.dose: 5–10 IU slowly IV, then 20 IU in 1 L isotonic crystalloid over 2 hours (MSF regimen)
oxytocin-pph.duration: Initial infusion over 2 h; reassess continuously and prescribe further treatment according to response
oxytocin-pph.preparation: With 10 IU/mL stock, 20 IU = 2 mL added to 1 L sodium chloride 0.9% or Ringer lactate. Pump 500 mL/hour = 10 IU/hour. Include this litre in total resuscitation fluid
oxytocin-pph.maxDose: MSF maximum total oxytocin 60 IU; avoid rapid boluses and excessive fluid
monitoring: Quantified blood loss, uterine tone, BP/pulse, perfusion and urine output; record every dose and time
Persistent shock or bleeding needs source control and blood products in parallel; do not wait for all drug doses
Fluid balance, sodium if prolonged/high-volume treatment; cardiac disease needs a separately prescribed concentrated infusion
contraindications: Rapid IV injection can cause hypotension/tachycardia
Monitor fluid overload, especially pre-eclampsia or cardiac disease

oxytocin-augmentation.indication: Inadequate contractions after obstetric assessment; exclude obstruction and contraindications to vaginal birth
oxytocin-augmentation.dose: Start 1–4 milliunits/min; increase in 1–2 milliunits/min steps no more frequently than every 20 min (specified product label)
oxytocin-augmentation.frequency: Continuous, titrated to contractions and fetal heart rate
oxytocin-augmentation.duration: Until effective labour/birth or an indication to stop; reassess the indication throughout
oxytocin-augmentation.preparation: 5 IU in FINAL 500 mL isotonic fluid = 10 milliunits/mL: 1 milliunit/min = 6 mL/hour; 2 = 12; 4 = 24. Use a dedicated labelled pump
oxytocin-augmentation.maxDose: 20 milliunits/min for the cited term-labour product regimen; higher rates require a different expressly authorised protocol
monitoring: Continuous fetal monitoring and contraction frequency; target 3–4 contractions/10 min
Stop/reduce for excessive contractions or abnormal fetal heart rate; evaluate immediately
contraindications: Obstruction, fetal compromise requiring birth, contraindication to vaginal birth or uterine rupture risk
Never give as an IV push; wait at least 4 h after oral misoprostol per its product label

txa-pph.indication: PPH of any cause; first dose as soon as possible and WITHIN 3 h of birth
txa-pph.dose: 1 g IV over 10 min; repeat 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 min OR restarts within 24 h
txa-pph.frequency: One initial dose; at most one additional 1 g dose under those criteria
txa-pph.duration: Acute PPH treatment, maximum 2 doses in this regimen
txa-pph.preparation: 100 mg/mL: 1 g = 10 mL. Give no faster than 1 mL/min, or dilute in compatible sodium chloride 0.9% and infuse over 10 min. Clearly label IV ONLY; never intrathecal
txa-pph.maxDose: 2 g total. The 24 h repeat rule does NOT permit a first dose after the 3 h window
monitoring: Quantified blood loss, uterine tone, BP/pulse, perfusion and urine output; record every dose and time
Persistent shock or bleeding needs source control and blood products in parallel; do not wait for all drug doses
contraindications: Clear contraindication to antifibrinolysis, such as a known thromboembolic event during pregnancy; renal dysfunction needs dose review
txa-pph.renalHepatic: Renal clearance: assess renal function and seek dose advice with impairment; do not repeatedly dose without review

txa-hmb.indication: Heavy uterine bleeding unrelated to pregnancy after assessment
txa-hmb.frequency: Three times daily; if necessary up to four times daily
txa-hmb.duration: During bleeding only; stop when bleeding stops, maximum 5 days per episode
txa-hmb.preparation: Swallow the prescribed 500 mg tablets with water; confirm pregnancy exclusion when clinically relevant
txa-hmb.maxDose: 4 g/day and no more than 5 days per episode
monitoring: Bleeding response, Hb/iron deficiency; investigate persistent or changed bleeding
contraindications: Current or previous thromboembolic disease, severe renal impairment or seizure history
Combined oestrogen use needs an individual thrombosis-risk assessment

carboprost-pph.indication: Refractory atonic PPH after first-line uterotonic; do not use for trauma or retained tissue alone
carboprost-pph.frequency: Repeat according to response at intervals of 15–90 min; NEVER sooner than 15 min
carboprost-pph.duration: Acute rescue; ongoing bleeding requires parallel tamponade/surgery
carboprost-pph.preparation: 250 micrograms/mL: draw 1 mL undiluted. Verify units carefully: micrograms, not milligrams. Do not administer IV
monitoring: Quantified blood loss, uterine tone, BP/pulse, perfusion and urine output; record every dose and time
Persistent shock or bleeding needs source control and blood products in parallel; do not wait for all drug doses
Respiratory status/bronchospasm, BP, vomiting/diarrhoea
contraindications: Asthma or significant active pulmonary disease; active cardiac, renal or hepatic disease
Do not persist with repeated injections in a deteriorating patient

methylergometrine-pph.indication: Atonic PPH after delivery; this is NOT the same formulation/dose as ergometrine
methylergometrine-pph.frequency: May repeat after 2–4 h if necessary, following reassessment
methylergometrine-pph.duration: Acute treatment after birth; do not prescribe repeated doses while delaying haemorrhage control
methylergometrine-pph.preparation: 0.2 mg/mL: 1 mL IM. Check the ampoule for the actual drug name. Routine IV use is avoided because of sudden hypertension/stroke risk
methylergometrine-pph.maxDose: 0.2 mg per injection; further doses require documented reassessment. No invented 15-minute repeat course
monitoring: Quantified blood loss, uterine tone, BP/pulse, perfusion and urine output; record every dose and time
Persistent shock or bleeding needs source control and blood products in parallel; do not wait for all drug doses
BP before each dose; chest pain, vasospasm, headache and neurological symptoms
contraindications: Hypertension/pre-eclampsia/eclampsia; vascular or significant cardiac disease; before delivery of the last baby
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; do not combine ergot preparations
notes: The product label advises no breastfeeding during treatment and for at least 12 h after the last dose; express/discard milk during that interval.

ergometrine-pph.indication: Alternative uterotonic for atonic PPH; use this row only when the ampoule is ERGOMETRINE
ergometrine-pph.dose: 200–500 micrograms IM; severe haemorrhage option 250–500 micrograms slow IV by a senior clinician
ergometrine-pph.route: IM; slow IV only for severe haemorrhage
ergometrine-pph.frequency: Initial dose followed by reassessment; select another indicated intervention for continuing bleeding
ergometrine-pph.duration: Acute post-birth treatment; no routine multi-day course in this emergency row
ergometrine-pph.preparation: 500 micrograms/mL formulation: 500 micrograms = 1 mL. For IV use the cited label permits dilution to 5 mL with sodium chloride 0.9%; administer slowly with BP monitoring
ergometrine-pph.maxDose: 500 micrograms per dose in this label; do not substitute the methylergometrine schedule or invent a cumulative ceiling
monitoring: Quantified blood loss, uterine tone, BP/pulse, perfusion and urine output; record every dose and time
Persistent shock or bleeding needs source control and blood products in parallel; do not wait for all drug doses
BP before and after injection; chest pain, severe headache, peripheral ischaemia
contraindications: Hypertension/pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, severe cardiac/vascular disease, severe renal/hepatic impairment
Never use before delivery of the last baby

misoprostol-pph.indication: Atonic PPH when IV oxytocin is unavailable or bleeding does not respond; additional uterotonic selection depends on drugs already given
misoprostol-pph.route: Sublingual; rectal if sublingual administration is not feasible
misoprostol-pph.duration: One acute dose; arrange further haemorrhage control if bleeding continues
misoprostol-pph.preparation: Four 200-microgram tablets = 800 micrograms; place under the tongue. Do not confuse this with the 25-microgram labour-induction dose
misoprostol-pph.maxDose: 800 micrograms in this rescue regimen; do not automatically repeat
monitoring: Quantified blood loss, uterine tone, BP/pulse, perfusion and urine output; record every dose and time
Persistent shock or bleeding needs source control and blood products in parallel; do not wait for all drug doses
Temperature, shivering, gastrointestinal effects; distinguish drug fever from ongoing sepsis
contraindications: Do not use PPH dosing before birth of the baby

labetalol-iv.indication: Persistent severe hypertension in pregnancy or postpartum (systolic ≥160 OR diastolic ≥110 mmHg)
labetalol-iv.dose: 20 mg over 2 min; reassess at 10 min, then 40 mg; further 80 mg doses at 10-min intervals if severe BP persists
labetalol-iv.duration: Acute control, then change to an appropriate oral regimen
labetalol-iv.preparation: 5 mg/mL stock: 20 mg = 4 mL, 40 mg = 8 mL, 80 mg = 16 mL. Give each dose slowly, record cumulative dose and check the stock strength
labetalol-iv.maxDose: 300 mg cumulative in the cited Indian CEmONC regimen; seek escalation before continuing beyond it
monitoring: Check BP and pulse before and after each acute dose; fetal monitoring when appropriate
Persistent severe BP despite the initial sequence requires senior/anaesthetic review, a different agent and HDU-level monitoring; avoid uncontrolled stacking
contraindications: Asthma, bradycardia/heart block or decompensated heart failure

labetalol-oral.dose: Start 100 mg twice daily; increase by 100–200 mg increments according to BP; higher daily doses divided three times daily
labetalol-oral.frequency: Twice daily initially; three divided doses if higher doses needed
labetalol-oral.duration: Continue while clinically required; titrate down rather than stop abruptly, with a postpartum review plan
labetalol-oral.preparation: 100 mg or 200 mg tablets; prescribe the strength, dose and administration times
monitoring: BP/heart rate, postural symptoms; neonatal glucose/heart-rate observation after late-pregnancy exposure
contraindications: Asthma, heart block, marked bradycardia, decompensated heart failure

hydralazine-iv.dose: 5 mg slowly IV over 2–4 min; reassess for 20 min and repeat 5 mg if still severe
hydralazine-iv.frequency: Every 20 min if required after reassessment
hydralazine-iv.duration: Acute control; transition to oral therapy once stable
hydralazine-iv.preparation: Reconstitute a 20 mg vial with 1 mL water for injection, then add 9 mL sodium chloride 0.9%: 2 mg/mL. A 5 mg dose = 2.5 mL. Use immediately; do not mix with other drugs
hydralazine-iv.maxDose: 20 mg cumulative in this MSF bolus regimen
monitoring: Check BP and pulse before and after each acute dose; fetal monitoring when appropriate
Persistent severe BP despite the initial sequence requires senior/anaesthetic review, a different agent and HDU-level monitoring; avoid uncontrolled stacking
contraindications: Marked hypotension, severe tachycardia or coronary ischaemia; use cautiously in cardiac disease

nifedipine-acute.indication: Acute severe hypertension when oral dosing is appropriate
nifedipine-acute.dose: 10 mg swallowed; reassess at 20 min and give another 10–20 mg if still severe
nifedipine-acute.frequency: Reassess after each 20-minute interval; switch/escalate when the initial-course limit is reached
nifedipine-acute.duration: Acute sequence, followed by senior review and a separately prescribed maintenance regimen
nifedipine-acute.preparation: Use immediate-release oral tablets/capsules; swallow whole. NEVER sublingual administration; do not use an extended-release tablet as a rapid-loading substitute
nifedipine-acute.maxDose: 30 mg cumulative for the NHM prose-based initial course; seek senior selection of another agent rather than continuing oral loading
monitoring: Check BP and pulse before and after each acute dose; fetal monitoring when appropriate
Persistent severe BP despite the initial sequence requires senior/anaesthetic review, a different agent and HDU-level monitoring; avoid uncontrolled stacking
contraindications: Hypotension, significant aortic stenosis or acute cardiac compromise
Magnesium co-administration requires close respiratory/neuromuscular and BP monitoring; follow the named unit protocol
notes: NHM CEmONC contains an internal discrepancy: its prose caps the initial course at 30 mg, while the adjacent flowchart shows 10 mg then 20 mg then 20 mg. The app uses the 30 mg prose limit with prompt escalation; confirm the locally approved sequence.

nifedipine-maintenance.dose: Start sustained-release nifedipine 10 mg twice daily; titrate according to BP and the exact release formulation
nifedipine-maintenance.frequency: Twice daily for the cited sustained-release regimen
nifedipine-maintenance.duration: While hypertension persists; reassess after birth and reduce when BP allows
nifedipine-maintenance.preparation: Use the specified sustained-release tablet, swallowed intact. Other extended-release products may use different strengths/schedules; do not interchange them or use them for acute oral loading.
nifedipine-maintenance.maxDose: 80 mg/day for the NHM CEmONC sustained-release regimen
monitoring: BP, headache, flushing, oedema and pulse
contraindications: Maternal hypotension or significant cardiac outflow obstruction

nifedipine-tocolysis.indication: Selected threatened preterm labour to gain time for steroids/transfer, without infection, major bleeding or a reason for immediate birth
nifedipine-tocolysis.dose: 10 mg orally; if contractions persist repeat every 15 min up to four loading doses; then 20 mg every 6 h
nifedipine-tocolysis.frequency: Loading as specified, then every 6 h
nifedipine-tocolysis.preparation: 10 mg immediate-release tablet/capsule; check BP before dosing and confirm the formulation
nifedipine-tocolysis.maxDose: 40 mg loading; maintenance 80 mg/day; stop after 48 h
monitoring: BP/pulse, contraction frequency and fetal heart rate; stop for hypotension or ischaemic chest pain
contraindications: Systolic BP <90 mmHg, severe cardiac disease
MSF advises against concurrent magnesium; if magnesium is needed, use the agreed obstetric/anaesthetic protocol and do not combine regimens casually

methyldopa.indication: Maintenance hypertension during pregnancy; not emergency BP rescue
methyldopa.dose: 250 mg twice or three times daily for 2 days; increase by 250 mg every 2–3 days to response
methyldopa.frequency: Two or three divided doses initially; prescribed divided doses thereafter
methyldopa.duration: During pregnancy if required; NICE recommends stopping within 2 days after birth and substituting another agent if needed
methyldopa.preparation: 250 mg tablets. Do not abruptly discontinue ongoing therapy without a replacement/reduction plan
monitoring: BP, sedation/mood; blood count and LFTs for fever, jaundice or suspected toxicity
contraindications: Active liver disease, previous methyldopa hepatitis, severe depression
notes: Postpartum stopping recommendation: NICE NG133.

aspirin-pe.indication: NICE regimen for pre-eclampsia prevention in women meeting high/moderate-risk criteria
aspirin-pe.duration: From 12 weeks until birth (NICE NG133); use a single named prevention protocol
aspirin-pe.preparation: Swallow the prescribed low-dose tablet; do not substitute analgesic-dose aspirin
monitoring: Adherence, bleeding, allergy and the evolving obstetric risk assessment
contraindications: Aspirin allergy/NSAID hypersensitivity, active significant bleeding or relevant bleeding disorder
notes: Some other named prevention protocols stop at 36 weeks. Choose and document one start/stop protocol rather than prescribing a fixed number of weeks irrespective of gestation.

enoxaparin-treatment.indication: Confirmed or strongly suspected acute VTE in pregnancy unless anticoagulation is contraindicated
enoxaparin-treatment.duration: For the remainder of pregnancy and at least 6 weeks postpartum; at least 3 months total anticoagulation
enoxaparin-treatment.preparation: Use a graduated prefilled syringe of the correct mg strength; inject SC, not IM. Do not interchange mg, mL and anti-Xa units
enoxaparin-treatment.maxDose: Weight-based therapeutic dose; renal dysfunction changes the regimen, not an arbitrary fixed maximum
monitoring: Baseline CBC/platelets, renal/liver function and bleeding risk; clinical response
Routine anti-Xa monitoring is not needed for most women; consider extremes of weight, renal impairment or recurrent VTE
Stop therapeutic LMWH at least 24 h before planned neuraxial procedures; anaesthetic staff must prescribe postpartum restart using puncture time, catheter removal and haemostasis
contraindications: Active major bleeding, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or imminent urgent surgery without an anticoagulation plan
enoxaparin-treatment.renalHepatic: CrCl <30 mL/min: specialist regimen; consider IV unfractionated heparin when rapid reversal is needed

enoxaparin-prophylaxis.indication: Risk-assessed obstetric thromboprophylaxis; standard-weight example, NOT VTE treatment
enoxaparin-prophylaxis.dose: 40 mg for a woman weighing 50–90 kg; other weight bands require the RCOG weight table
enoxaparin-prophylaxis.duration: According to the documented risk assessment: commonly 10 days after birth or 6 weeks for high risk; antenatal use when indicated
enoxaparin-prophylaxis.preparation: 40 mg/0.4 mL prefilled product: use the prescribed syringe SC. Confirm its actual concentration; do not give IM
enoxaparin-prophylaxis.maxDose: 40 mg/day applies ONLY to this standard-weight prophylactic row; renal impairment and weight extremes require adjustment
monitoring: Reassess VTE and bleeding risk after birth, surgery, admission or clinical change
At least 12 h between prophylactic LMWH and neuraxial placement; postpartum restart needs an anaesthetic plan, adequate haemostasis and consideration of time since puncture/catheter removal
contraindications: Active bleeding, HIT or neuraxial timing contraindication
enoxaparin-prophylaxis.renalHepatic: Reduced renal function requires a different dose/agent; do not reuse a standard prophylactic syringe without review

metformin.indication: Selected GDM/type 2 diabetes; assess glucose, renal function and suitability for metformin versus insulin
metformin.dose: Week 1: 500 mg with breakfast; week 2: 500 mg twice daily; increase by 500 mg/week if tolerated and needed
metformin.frequency: Once daily initially, then twice daily with meals
metformin.duration: While indicated and tolerated; GDM treatment is normally stopped after birth, with a diabetes follow-up plan
metformin.preparation: 500 mg tablets taken with meals. Use slower titration for gastrointestinal intolerance; do not silently substitute a modified-release product
metformin.maxDose: 2 g/day (1 g twice daily) for this MSF regimen
monitoring: Fasting and post-meal glucose; renal function before treatment and with acute illness; B12 with long-term use
Escalate to insulin when glucose targets are not reached or metformin is unsuitable
contraindications: DKA, hypoxia, major dehydration or severe renal impairment
notes: NICE NG3 permits metformin in selected pregnancies; placental transfer and treatment alternatives should be discussed.
metformin.renalHepatic: Avoid if eGFR <30; reduced dosing/closer review with moderate impairment; withhold during acute dehydration, hypoxia or renal deterioration

insulin-nph.drug: NPH (isophane) insulin with prescribed mealtime insulin
insulin-nph.indication: Pregnancy diabetes: match basal and meal insulin to the glucose pattern
insulin-nph.dose: Patient-specific dose in UNITS; NPH once or twice daily, with separately prescribed meal doses if needed. A universal 0.3-units/kg starting prescription is not appropriate for every GDM pattern
insulin-nph.frequency: NPH once/twice daily; short-acting insulin before meals according to its formulation
insulin-nph.duration: Continue and titrate throughout pregnancy; reduce/review promptly after birth. Type 1 diabetes always requires basal insulin
insulin-nph.preparation: Use U-100 insulin with a matching insulin syringe/pen. Gently resuspend NPH until uniform. NPH is NEVER IV. If mixing compatible human insulins, draw clear short-acting insulin before cloudy NPH
insulin-nph.maxDose: No universal fixed maximum: titrate the prescribed units against glucose and hypoglycaemia, with the diabetes team
monitoring: Record the actual basal/meal doses in the patient plan; monitor fasting, premeal/postmeal glucose or CGM
Review patterns rather than a single high value; teach injection technique, recognition/treatment of hypoglycaemia and sick-day ketone testing
NICE targets, if achievable without problematic hypoglycaemia: fasting <5.3 mmol/L, 1-h postmeal <7.8 or 2-h <6.4; keep glucose >4 mmol/L on insulin
contraindications: Current hypoglycaemia requires treatment and dose review; do not omit basal insulin in type 1 diabetes
notes: The linked NICE NG3 guidance provides pregnancy targets and treatment selection. The dose must be prescribed individually; this is an explicit dosing constraint, not a missing fixed dose.

betamethasone-antenatal.indication: Imminent preterm birth within the guideline gestational window; do not delay urgent maternal/fetal delivery
betamethasone-antenatal.dose: 12 mg IM, then 12 mg IM 24 hours later
betamethasone-antenatal.duration: One 24 mg course. Consider only ONE repeat course under NICE criteria; not routine weekly courses
betamethasone-antenatal.preparation: Confirm product strength: for 6 mg/mL, 12 mg = 2 mL; volumes differ by formulation. Use the obstetric IM preparation
betamethasone-antenatal.maxDose: 24 mg/course; NICE permits no more than 2 courses in total under its repeat-course criteria
monitoring: Glucose monitoring and an insulin-adjustment plan in diabetes; assess infection and timing of birth
contraindications: Do not delay lifesaving delivery to complete steroids; do not use a blanket “infection contraindication” without senior assessment
notes: NICE offers at 24+0–33+6 weeks, considers 34+0–35+6; individual discussion at 22+0–23+6. Repeat: <34 weeks, prior course >7 days ago and very high risk of birth in 48 h.

dexamethasone-antenatal.dose: 6 mg IM every 12 h for four doses
dexamethasone-antenatal.duration: 24 mg total over 36 h; ONE course, subject to the same repeat-course restrictions
dexamethasone-antenatal.preparation: Check the injectable product: if 4 mg/mL, 6 mg = 1.5 mL; other strengths require recalculation. Give IM for this antenatal regimen
dexamethasone-antenatal.maxDose: Four 6 mg doses = 24 mg/course; do not combine with a full betamethasone course
monitoring: Maternal glucose, infection assessment and birth timing; diabetes team plan
contraindications: Do not prolong an unsafe pregnancy to finish the course

cefazolin-cs.indication: Surgical prophylaxis, not treatment of established infection
cefazolin-cs.dose: 2 g IV; 3 g for weight ≥120 kg in the cited surgical prophylaxis standard
cefazolin-cs.frequency: Once, completed within 60 min before incision; redose for a prolonged operation or major blood loss
cefazolin-cs.duration: Single perioperative prophylaxis course; do not continue routine postoperative doses without an infection indication
cefazolin-cs.preparation: Reconstitute and dilute the specific cefazolin vial according to its label; prepare a compatible IV infusion and administer over 30 min for the cited formulation. Never use an IM lidocaine diluent IV
cefazolin-cs.maxDose: Initial 2 g (or 3 g ≥120 kg); redose cefazolin at 4 h if indicated, earlier after major blood loss per anaesthetic plan
monitoring: Allergy history, time relative to incision, operation duration and blood loss
contraindications: Severe beta-lactam allergy requires an alternative COMBINATION regimen, not clindamycin alone by default
notes: For a severe beta-lactam allergy, the cited prophylaxis standard uses clindamycin 900 mg IV PLUS gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV as a single pre-incision regimen. Confirm dosing weight/renal risk.

ampicillin-chorio.indication: Intra-amniotic infection, in combination with gentamicin; add anaerobic cover for caesarean according to the chosen guideline
ampicillin-chorio.duration: Continue through birth with postpartum review; the cited Malaysian NAG continues until afebrile/asymptomatic ≥48 h. Other national protocols shorten postpartum treatment after clinical recovery
ampicillin-chorio.preparation: Reconstitute the actual vial per label; dilute each adult dose in 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9% or glucose 5% and infuse over 30 min. Use a separate line/flush from gentamicin
ampicillin-chorio.maxDose: 8 g/day in this 2 g every-6-h regimen; renal impairment requires adjustment
monitoring: Temperature, pulse, BP, uterine tenderness, fetal heart rate, cultures and renal function
contraindications: Penicillin anaphylaxis; check severe delayed beta-lactam reactions
notes: This is not GBS prophylaxis and is not ampicillin monotherapy. The postpartum duration differs between guidelines; record the local choice explicitly.

ampicillin-gbs.indication: GBS prevention during labour when prophylaxis is indicated
ampicillin-gbs.dose: 2 g IV initially, then 1 g IV
ampicillin-gbs.frequency: Initial 2 g load, then 1 g every 4 hours
ampicillin-gbs.duration: Continue UNTIL BIRTH; this is not a multi-day infection-treatment course
ampicillin-gbs.preparation: Reconstitute according to the vial; dilute the adult dose in compatible fluid and infuse over 30 min. Do not mix with gentamicin
ampicillin-gbs.maxDose: 2 g loading, then 1 g per subsequent dose until birth
monitoring: Penicillin allergy, dose times and delivery time; do not delay necessary obstetric intervention solely to complete antibiotic hours
contraindications: Penicillin anaphylaxis or severe delayed beta-lactam reaction
notes: Penicillin G is dosed in MILLION UNITS; its 5-million-unit loading schedule must not be copied as grams of ampicillin.

gentamicin-obstetric.indication: Combination therapy for chorioamnionitis, postpartum endometritis or septic miscarriage
gentamicin-obstetric.dose: 5 mg/kg using the approved aminoglycoside dosing weight
gentamicin-obstetric.frequency: Every 24 h initially if renal function allows; subsequent interval depends on drug levels and renal function
gentamicin-obstetric.duration: Daily review; limit unnecessary exposure, stop or narrow after source control and clinical recovery. Duration follows the infection, not a universal 48–72 h rule
gentamicin-obstetric.preparation: 40 mg/mL stock: volume in mL = prescribed mg ÷40. Dilute the adult dose in 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9%/glucose 5%; infuse over 30 min. Use a separate line/flush from beta-lactams
gentamicin-obstetric.maxDose: Weight-based; do not apply total body weight uncritically in obesity. Withhold/review further doses for accumulating levels or renal deterioration
monitoring: Baseline and serial creatinine/urine output; drug-level monitoring using the hospital once-daily schedule
Ask about tinnitus, hearing change or vertigo; stop and review suspected ototoxicity
contraindications: Aminoglycoside allergy; myasthenia gravis, AKI, prior auditory/vestibular toxicity require specialist assessment
gentamicin-obstetric.renalHepatic: Adjust interval/dose to renal function and measured levels; do not keep automatic daily dosing in AKI

ceftriaxone-gonorrhoea.indication: Gonococcal cervicitis/urethritis; add pregnancy-appropriate chlamydia treatment if not excluded
ceftriaxone-gonorrhoea.dose: 500 mg IM once if weight <150 kg; 1 g IM once if ≥150 kg
ceftriaxone-gonorrhoea.duration: Single treatment dose; partner management, test-of-cure when indicated and retesting remain necessary
ceftriaxone-gonorrhoea.preparation: Use the IM diluent specified for the exact vial; lidocaine-containing IM solution must NEVER be given IV. Reconstitution volumes vary by brand
ceftriaxone-gonorrhoea.maxDose: 1 g for the ≥150 kg group in this CDC regimen
monitoring: Allergy, pregnancy and chlamydia status; retest at 3 months, and pharyngeal infection test-of-cure at 7–14 days
contraindications: Severe cephalosporin allergy requires a specific alternative and specialist advice in pregnancy

ceftriaxone-pid-im.indication: Mild/moderate PID in a NON-PREGNANT patient suitable for outpatient treatment
ceftriaxone-pid-im.dose: 500 mg IM once, PLUS doxycycline 100 mg twice daily AND metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 14 days
ceftriaxone-pid-im.duration: One ceftriaxone dose; oral partners for 14 days; reassess within 72 h
ceftriaxone-pid-im.preparation: Use the vial-specific IM reconstitution. Do not use lidocaine-containing IM solution IV
ceftriaxone-pid-im.maxDose: If ≥150 kg with documented gonorrhoea, ceftriaxone 1 g IM (CDC). Do not repeat daily as an outpatient substitute for reassessment
monitoring: Clinical improvement within 72 h, STI results, adherence, partner treatment and pregnancy test
contraindications: Pregnancy, tubo-ovarian abscess, severe illness/vomiting or uncertain surgical diagnosis usually requires admission; this outpatient doxycycline regimen is unsuitable

ceftriaxone-pid-iv.indication: Hospitalised PID, with appropriate combination antibiotics
ceftriaxone-pid-iv.dose: 1 g IV daily, PLUS doxycycline 100 mg twice daily AND metronidazole 500 mg twice daily
ceftriaxone-pid-iv.frequency: Ceftriaxone every 24 h; partners every 12 h
ceftriaxone-pid-iv.duration: Switch after clinical improvement (usually 24–48 h) to appropriate oral therapy to COMPLETE 14 days; abscess needs adequate anaerobic cover
ceftriaxone-pid-iv.preparation: Reconstitute with water for injection per product, dilute in 100 mL compatible sodium chloride 0.9%/glucose 5% and infuse over 30 min. No calcium-containing diluent
ceftriaxone-pid-iv.maxDose: 1 g/day in this CDC PID regimen; do not omit the combination partners
monitoring: Clinical response, cultures, oral tolerance and abscess/source-control assessment
contraindications: Pregnancy requires an obstetric/infection-specialist regimen; do not automatically continue doxycycline

ceftriaxone-pyelonephritis.indication: Selected inpatient pyelonephritis in pregnancy, guided by cultures and resistance
ceftriaxone-pyelonephritis.duration: Review IV therapy by 48 h; step down when improving. ACOG uses 14 days TOTAL therapy for pregnancy pyelonephritis
ceftriaxone-pyelonephritis.preparation: Use water for reconstitution and a compatible non-calcium IV diluent; adult infusion example 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9% over 30 min. Do not give lidocaine-containing IM solution IV
ceftriaxone-pyelonephritis.maxDose: 2 g/day for this row; renal/hepatic dysfunction and severe infection need individual review
monitoring: Vitals, sepsis features, renal function, cultures and clinical response within 48–72 h
contraindications: Cephalosporin anaphylaxis; do not use nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin as renal-parenchymal step-down agents
notes: The NICE NG111 pregnancy table usually uses cefuroxime; this is the ACOG-compatible ceftriaxone option, not a claim that every guideline chooses the same drug.

doxycycline-chlamydia.indication: Chlamydial infection in a non-pregnant adult
doxycycline-chlamydia.preparation: Take with a full glass of water while upright; stay upright for at least 1 h. Separate iron, calcium, zinc and antacids by ≥2 h
monitoring: Adherence, pregnancy status, partner treatment and retesting at approximately 3 months
contraindications: Pregnancy: use a pregnancy-recommended regimen such as azithromycin rather than this row

doxycycline-pid.indication: Non-pregnant PID; combine with ceftriaxone and metronidazole
doxycycline-pid.preparation: Oral route is effective when tolerated; use a full glass of water and remain upright. Separate from polyvalent cations
monitoring: Clinical response within 72 h and oral tolerance; check pregnancy and partner management
contraindications: Do not apply the non-pregnant PID regimen in pregnancy

metronidazole-bv.indication: Symptomatic BV, including pregnancy where treatment is indicated
metronidazole-bv.preparation: One 500 mg tablet each dose. Alternative formulations/regimens must be prescribed separately
metronidazole-bv.maxDose: 1 g/day for 7 days in this CDC regimen
monitoring: Symptoms and tolerance; recurrent symptoms need reassessment, not indefinite repeat courses
contraindications: Nitroimidazole allergy; review warfarin, lithium and severe hepatic disease
notes: CDC does not require routine alcohol abstinence on evidence of a disulfiram-like interaction; product leaflets may give different advice. Follow the dispensed product instructions and discuss the difference.

metronidazole-trichomonas.preparation: One 500 mg tablet each dose; assess vomiting/adherence
monitoring: Treat partner(s), avoid sex until both treatment courses complete and symptoms resolve, and retest women at about 3 months
contraindications: Nitroimidazole allergy; review interactions and hepatic impairment

metronidazole-pid.indication: Anaerobic cover in the complete CDC PID regimen
metronidazole-pid.preparation: One 500 mg tablet twice daily, with doxycycline and the appropriate cephalosporin regimen
monitoring: Clinical response within 72 h and tolerance
contraindications: Nitroimidazole allergy; review interactions and severe hepatic impairment

metronidazole-iv.indication: Combination treatment of selected septic miscarriage/endometritis or caesarean chorioamnionitis
metronidazole-iv.duration: Review daily and switch to oral when feasible; duration is source-specific: uncomplicated infection recovery versus septic miscarriage (10–14 days in Malaysian NAG)
metronidazole-iv.preparation: Ready-to-use 500 mg/100 mL (5 mg/mL) bag infused over 30 min; do not add other drugs to the bag
metronidazole-iv.maxDose: 1.5 g/day in this regimen; severe hepatic impairment requires reduction
monitoring: Clinical response, LFTs in prolonged treatment, interacting anticoagulants and neuropathy with prolonged exposure
contraindications: Nitroimidazole allergy; severe hepatic impairment requires a reduced regimen
metronidazole-iv.renalHepatic: In severe hepatic impairment the cited MSF monograph reduces the daily dose to one third

azithromycin-chlamydia.indication: Recommended CDC regimen for chlamydia in pregnancy
azithromycin-chlamydia.duration: Single dose; test-of-cure at approximately 4 weeks and retest at 3 months
azithromycin-chlamydia.preparation: Two 500 mg tablets (or four 250 mg tablets) taken together; check formulation instructions. Persistent vomiting requires reassessment
monitoring: Partner treatment, adherence/retained dose, symptoms; do not test NAAT too early after treatment
contraindications: Macrolide allergy; QT prolongation, electrolyte disturbance or interacting QT-prolonging drugs need review

erythromycin-pprom.indication: Confirmed PPROM without established infection or another indication for immediate birth
erythromycin-pprom.duration: Maximum 10 days OR until established labour, whichever occurs first (NICE NG25)
erythromycin-pprom.preparation: 250 mg tablets; confirm the erythromycin salt and avoid erythromycin estolate in pregnancy. Do not substitute co-amoxiclav for latency prophylaxis
erythromycin-pprom.maxDose: 1 g/day for at most 10 days in this regimen
monitoring: Temperature, pulse, uterine tenderness, fetal status and drug tolerance; infection changes management
contraindications: Macrolide allergy; QT prolongation and interacting drugs; do not use latency antibiotics to defer delivery in sepsis

misoprostol-abortion.indication: After appropriate eligibility, pregnancy-location assessment and consent; comply with India MTP law and approved service arrangements
misoprostol-abortion.frequency: Initial dose once; additional doses require a defined abortion-care regimen and reassessment
misoprostol-abortion.duration: Initial combined course over 1–2 days; confirm completion using the service follow-up plan
misoprostol-abortion.preparation: Four 200-microgram tablets = 800 micrograms. Use the prescribed route; do not substitute the labour-induction dose
misoprostol-abortion.maxDose: WHO permits repeat doses when required without a universal fixed maximum; do not import the ≥12-week 400-microgram schedule into this <12-week row
monitoring: Expected bleeding/pain, heavy bleeding, infection signs and pregnancy resolution; persistent pain or symptoms requires ectopic assessment
contraindications: Suspected ectopic pregnancy, haemodynamic instability, uncontrolled major bleeding; urgent assessment rather than outpatient dosing

misoprostol-missed.indication: NICE NG126 medical management of confirmed missed miscarriage
misoprostol-missed.dose: 800 micrograms 48 h after mifepristone 200 mg orally, unless the sac has already passed
misoprostol-missed.duration: Single initial combined course; review if bleeding has not started within 48 h of misoprostol
misoprostol-missed.preparation: Four 200-microgram tablets = 800 micrograms; provide analgesia and contact arrangements
misoprostol-missed.maxDose: 800 micrograms initially; further treatment follows reassessment rather than automatic repeat dosing
monitoring: Bleeding, pain, fever and haemodynamic symptoms; home urine pregnancy test at 3 weeks with assessment if positive or symptomatic
contraindications: Uncertain viability/location, suspected ectopic or uncontrolled bleeding

misoprostol-incomplete.indication: NICE NG126 medical management of confirmed incomplete miscarriage
misoprostol-incomplete.dose: 600 micrograms (800 micrograms may be used to align local protocols)
misoprostol-incomplete.duration: Single initial treatment; follow-up and further intervention depend on symptoms/completion
misoprostol-incomplete.preparation: 600 micrograms = three 200-microgram tablets; 800 micrograms = four. Do NOT add mifepristone for incomplete miscarriage
misoprostol-incomplete.maxDose: One initial 600/800-microgram dose; reassess persistent bleeding or retained tissue
monitoring: Bleeding/pain, fever and urine pregnancy test at 3 weeks; positive test or concerning symptoms requires reassessment
contraindications: Instability, major haemorrhage, infection requiring source control or uncertain diagnosis

misoprostol-iol.indication: Unscarred uterus, live fetus and an approved hospital induction indication; cited 25-microgram product is for ≥37 weeks
misoprostol-iol.dose: 25 micrograms orally every 2 h (alternative product regimen: 50 micrograms every 4 h)
misoprostol-iol.frequency: Every 2 h for the 25-microgram regimen; stop further doses when labour begins or monitoring is abnormal
misoprostol-iol.duration: At most 24 h before review; stop for labour, tachysystole or fetal concern
misoprostol-iol.preparation: Use a manufactured 25-microgram tablet. The cited tablet score is NOT for splitting. Do not estimate 25 micrograms by casually cutting a 200-microgram tablet
misoprostol-iol.maxDose: 200 micrograms in 24 h; wait ≥4 h after the last dose before oxytocin
monitoring: Fetal heart rate and uterine contractions; hospital staff and emergency birth facilities available
contraindications: Prior caesarean/uterine scar, concurrent oxytocin, unexplained bleeding or fetal concern requiring delivery
notes: Vaginal and sublingual regimens have different intervals; do not copy this two-hour oral schedule to another route.

mifepristone-abortion.indication: Priming for a combined medical-abortion course <12 weeks, within the legal and service framework
mifepristone-abortion.frequency: Once, followed by misoprostol 800 micrograms 24–48 h later
mifepristone-abortion.duration: One combined course; confirmation of completion and emergency access are essential
mifepristone-abortion.preparation: One 200 mg tablet swallowed; arrange the exact subsequent misoprostol route, time and follow-up before treatment
mifepristone-abortion.maxDose: 200 mg in this priming regimen; not repeated daily
monitoring: Bleeding, pain, ongoing pregnancy symptoms and access to urgent review
contraindications: Suspected ectopic/molar pregnancy, chronic adrenal failure, long-term systemic corticosteroid therapy or significant bleeding/anticoagulation concerns
notes: A single dose does not require a routine breastfeeding interruption in the cited MSF monograph.

mifepristone-missed.indication: Confirmed missed miscarriage choosing NICE medical management
mifepristone-missed.dose: 200 mg, followed 48 h later by misoprostol 800 micrograms unless the sac has passed
mifepristone-missed.preparation: One 200 mg tablet; provide written timing and contact instructions. No mifepristone for incomplete miscarriage
monitoring: Symptoms, bleeding and subsequent completion assessment
contraindications: Ectopic pregnancy or unconfirmed diagnosis; adrenal insufficiency or long-term systemic steroids require review

methotrexate-ectopic.indication: Selected stable unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy with assured follow-up; NICE selection criteria apply
methotrexate-ectopic.frequency: Once on day 1; hCG on days 4 and 7
methotrexate-ectopic.duration: Weekly hCG thereafter until resolution; falling values do not eliminate rupture risk
methotrexate-ectopic.preparation: Record height and weight, calculate BSA and total mg. Cytotoxic pharmacy prepares the dose at the actual product concentration; independently verify prescribed mg and final mL. Do not reuse a fixed vial volume for every patient
methotrexate-ectopic.maxDose: No automatic repeat dose: <15% day-4-to-day-7 fall, plateau or rise requires senior reassessment for another dose or surgery
monitoring: Baseline CBC, liver/renal function and hCG; day-4/day-7 hCG, then weekly
Seek emergency care for worsening abdominal/shoulder-tip pain, dizziness, syncope or heavy bleeding
Avoid folate supplements, interacting NSAIDs and alcohol as advised; avoid conception for 3 months
contraindications: Rupture/instability, significant pain, inability to follow up, breastfeeding, significant cytopenia/liver/renal disease
NICE: fetal heartbeat, mass ≥35 mm or hCG ≥5000 IU/L favours surgery
notes: The NHS GGC protocol had a scheduled review date in September 2026; its local currency must be confirmed. NICE is used for eligibility.
If the day-4-to-day-7 fall is inadequate, do not automatically redose: reassess symptoms, hCG trend, eligibility and the need for surgery with a senior clinician.

ondansetron-oral.indication: Second-line nausea/vomiting or hyperemesis after assessment and discussion of benefits and small absolute fetal-risk signals
ondansetron-oral.dose: 4 mg every 8 h OR 8 mg every 12 h
ondansetron-oral.duration: Review daily during acute illness; reduce/stop as oral intake and symptoms improve rather than prescribe a fixed long course
ondansetron-oral.preparation: Use the prescribed tablet/orodispersible formulation; correct dehydration and electrolyte disturbance
ondansetron-oral.maxDose: 12 mg/day for 4 mg every 8 h OR 16 mg/day for 8 mg every 12 h; severe hepatic impairment max 8 mg/day
monitoring: Response, constipation, QT/ECG risk, potassium/magnesium and interacting QT-prolonging drugs
contraindications: Congenital long QT or significant electrolyte derangement needs correction/specialist review
notes: This obstetric guideline differs from the more restrictive MSF general ondansetron monograph; the app uses the RCOG HG pathway after counselling.

ondansetron-iv.indication: Second-line HG when oral treatment cannot be retained
ondansetron-iv.duration: Review daily; change to oral treatment when tolerated
ondansetron-iv.preparation: 2 mg/mL solution: 8 mg = 4 mL; dilute in compatible IV fluid according to the actual product label and infuse over 15 min, not rapid IV push
ondansetron-iv.maxDose: 16 mg/day in this RCOG HG regimen; severe hepatic impairment max 8 mg/day
monitoring: ECG/QT risk, potassium/magnesium, symptom control and constipation
contraindications: Correct significant electrolyte disturbance; review other QT-prolonging drugs

doxylamine-pyridoxine.indication: Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy: the cited product contains 10 mg/10 mg PER tablet
doxylamine-pyridoxine.dose: Day 1: two tablets at bedtime. If inadequate: day 3 add one morning tablet; day 4 may add one mid-afternoon tablet
doxylamine-pyridoxine.duration: Reassess during pregnancy; taper gradually when no longer needed
doxylamine-pyridoxine.preparation: 10 mg doxylamine +10 mg pyridoxine gastro-resistant tablets: swallow whole with water on an empty stomach. Do not crush, split or substitute a different-strength combination
doxylamine-pyridoxine.maxDose: 4 tablets/day: one morning, one mid-afternoon, two bedtime (40 mg/40 mg total)
monitoring: Sedation, symptom control, ability to eat/drink; avoid driving if drowsy
contraindications: MAO inhibitors; additive sedation with alcohol or other CNS depressants; breastfeeding requires product-specific advice

thiamine-hg-oral.indication: Prolonged vomiting or markedly reduced dietary intake; protect against thiamine deficiency
thiamine-hg-oral.duration: While vomiting/restricted intake persists; review nutritional recovery
thiamine-hg-oral.preparation: 100 mg tablet; if oral intake is unreliable, use prescribed parenteral supplementation BEFORE carbohydrate-containing fluids/nutrition
thiamine-hg-oral.maxDose: 300 mg/day for this oral supplementation regimen; suspected Wernicke disease requires a treatment regimen, not oral prophylaxis
monitoring: Dietary intake, weight, hydration; confusion, ataxia or eye-movement abnormalities require urgent assessment
contraindications: Do not treat suspected Wernicke encephalopathy with low-dose oral supplementation alone

thiamine-before-glucose.indication: Prolonged HG with inability to retain oral thiamine; before IV carbohydrate/nutrition
thiamine-before-glucose.dose: 100 mg parenteral thiamine as the initial supplementation dose; follow the local vitamin-B preparation for subsequent doses
thiamine-before-glucose.frequency: Before carbohydrate administration, with continued prescribed supplementation while intake is inadequate
thiamine-before-glucose.duration: Acute supplementation with daily nutritional review; change to oral 100 mg three times daily once retained
thiamine-before-glucose.preparation: If the product is 100 mg/2 mL, use one ampoule diluted as specified by its label and infuse very slowly over 30 min. Monitor for hypersensitivity
thiamine-before-glucose.maxDose: This is PREVENTION, not a Wernicke-treatment dose; suspected Wernicke needs urgent higher-dose specialist IV treatment
monitoring: Hypersensitivity, mental state, eye signs, gait, electrolytes and nutrition
contraindications: Do not delay lifesaving glucose in severe hypoglycaemia while searching for thiamine; give both promptly
notes: RCOG HG guidance describes oral thiamine or parenteral vitamin-B preparations; product composition and the ongoing course must be explicitly prescribed.

iron-fcm.indication: Laboratory-confirmed iron deficiency when oral iron is ineffective/intolerable or faster replacement is indicated; assess trimester and infection
iron-fcm.dose: Determine TOTAL need from Hb and weight, then give up to 20 mg/kg per infusion, not exceeding 1000 mg
iron-fcm.frequency: Repeat only if calculated deficit remains; additional dose at least 7 days later
iron-fcm.duration: Finite replacement course, not automatic weekly indefinite treatment
iron-fcm.preparation: 50 mg iron/mL: 1000 mg =20 mL. For >500–1000 mg dilute only in up to 250 mL sodium chloride 0.9% and infuse over at least 15 min. Do not dilute below 2 mg/mL
iron-fcm.maxDose: Lesser of 20 mg/kg or 1000 mg per infusion; maximum 1000 mg/week for adults in this Ferinject label
monitoring: Observe during and at least 30 min after infusion with anaphylaxis treatment available; monitor extravasation
Hb reassessment no earlier than 4 weeks after final dose; phosphate for repeated/high-dose courses or symptoms
contraindications: Non-iron-deficiency anaemia, iron overload or serious parenteral-iron hypersensitivity
Restrict pregnancy treatment to clear indications in the second/third trimester; avoid during ongoing bacteraemia
notes: Label total-need table: Hb <10 g/dL: 35–<70 kg 1500 mg, ≥70 kg 2000 mg. Hb 10–<14: 1000 mg and 1500 mg respectively. Hb ≥14: 500 mg. Below 35 kg: use the label weight-based calculation.
A 60 kg patient with Hb 8 g/dL therefore needs 1500 mg TOTAL, split 1000 mg then 500 mg ≥7 days later; 1000 mg is not automatically the full deficit.

levonorgestrel-ec.indication: After unprotected/inadequately protected intercourse; assess timing and offer the most effective suitable option
levonorgestrel-ec.duration: Single treatment, ideally ≤72 h; CDC allows emergency pills within 5 days, with reduced LNG effectiveness late in the window
levonorgestrel-ec.preparation: One 1.5 mg tablet (or two 0.75 mg tablets together). If vomiting within 3 h, repeat the dose promptly (CDC)
levonorgestrel-ec.maxDose: 1.5 mg initial course; enzyme-inducing medicines need a separate EC plan, preferably copper IUD when suitable
monitoring: Pregnancy test if no withdrawal bleed/period within 3 weeks; assess pregnancy symptoms or abdominal pain
Can start/resume hormonal contraception immediately after LNG, using condoms/abstinence for 7 days
contraindications: No benefit for an established pregnancy; does not protect against STIs or later unprotected intercourse
notes: Ulipristal or copper IUD may be more effective later in the 5-day window; do not apply ulipristal’s delayed hormonal-restart rule to LNG.

adrenaline-anaphylaxis.indication: Airway/breathing/circulation compromise from suspected anaphylaxis, including pregnancy
adrenaline-anaphylaxis.frequency: Repeat after 5 min if airway/breathing/circulation problems persist
adrenaline-anaphylaxis.duration: Continue emergency reassessment; refractory reaction after 2 appropriate IM doses needs expert IV-infusion/critical-care support
adrenaline-anaphylaxis.preparation: 1 mg/mL ampoule: 0.5 mL = 500 micrograms IM. Use mg/mL labels rather than ratio alone. NEVER give this IM-strength dose as an IV bolus
adrenaline-anaphylaxis.maxDose: No fixed total IM-dose ceiling while life-threatening features persist; repeat every 5 min and escalate
monitoring: Airway, breathing, BP/pulse, ECG and SpO2; pregnancy positioning and fetal assessment after maternal resuscitation
contraindications: No absolute contraindication to IM adrenaline in life-threatening anaphylaxis; do not withhold because of pregnancy
IV adrenaline requires an experienced clinician and monitored infusion; antihistamines/steroids do not replace adrenaline

adrenaline-arrest.indication: Maternal cardiac arrest following the adult ALS algorithm
adrenaline-arrest.frequency: Every 3–5 min during CPR; immediately for non-shockable rhythm, after the third shock for shockable rhythm
adrenaline-arrest.duration: During ongoing resuscitation, until ROSC or team decision
adrenaline-arrest.preparation: Use a 1 mg/10 mL (0.1 mg/mL) resuscitation syringe. If using 1 mg/mL stock, 1 mL diluted to FINAL 10 mL gives 0.1 mg/mL; independently check. Flush the IV/IO line and continue compressions
adrenaline-arrest.maxDose: 1 mg each scheduled dose; do not confuse with 0.5 mg IM anaphylaxis treatment
monitoring: Rhythm checks, CPR quality, capnography and reversible causes; use usual defibrillation energy in pregnancy
contraindications: Do not use an IM anaphylaxis approach to treat cardiac arrest; CPR/defibrillation are not delayed for drugs

glucose-severe-hypo.indication: Impaired consciousness or unsafe swallowing; never give oral fluid to an unconscious patient
glucose-severe-hypo.dose: 20 g glucose: 200 mL of 10% OR 100 mL of 20% solution
glucose-severe-hypo.frequency: Give over 10–15 min; recheck glucose at 10 min and repeat if still <4 mmol/L with reassessment
glucose-severe-hypo.duration: Acute rescue followed by longer-acting carbohydrate when awake and safe to swallow, or prescribed ongoing infusion
glucose-severe-hypo.preparation: 10% =100 mg/mL; 200 mL =20 g. 20% =200 mg/mL; 100 mL =20 g. Check IV patency and use a limited volume so a whole large bag cannot infuse accidentally
glucose-severe-hypo.maxDose: Reassess after each 20 g treatment; recurrent/prolonged hypoglycaemia needs monitored ongoing treatment
monitoring: Glucose 10 min after treatment, then serially until stable; consciousness, swallow and IV site
Identify missed food, insulin excess, renal failure or infection; do not omit basal insulin in type 1 diabetes
contraindications: Do not give oral sugar when swallowing is unsafe; hypertonic glucose extravasation can injure tissue

glucagon-hypo.indication: Severe insulin-associated hypoglycaemia when IV access is unavailable
glucagon-hypo.frequency: One rescue dose; obtain IV access and recheck glucose after 10 min
glucagon-hypo.duration: Bridge to reliable glucose delivery; give carbohydrate after recovery
glucagon-hypo.preparation: Reconstitute the 1 mg vial with its supplied solvent immediately before IM use; verify final dose
glucagon-hypo.maxDose: 1 mg initially; repeated glucagon may be ineffective and must not delay IV glucose
monitoring: Consciousness, glucose and nausea/vomiting; replenish carbohydrate once swallowing is safe
contraindications: Reduced effectiveness with prolonged starvation, liver disease, depleted glycogen or repeated episodes

insulin-dka.indication: Pregnancy DKA, including euglycaemic DKA; urgent monitored obstetric/diabetes care
insulin-dka.dose: 0.1 units/kg/hour IV; no routine IV insulin bolus. Consider 0.05 units/kg/hour once glucose <14 mmol/L alongside glucose infusion
insulin-dka.duration: Continue until ketones <0.6 mmol/L AND venous pH >7.3, clinical recovery and safe transition; not merely until glucose normalises
insulin-dka.preparation: Using U-100 SOLUBLE insulin: 50 units =0.5 mL; add to 49.5 mL sodium chloride 0.9% for FINAL 50 mL =1 unit/mL. At 0.1 units/kg/h, 70 kg =7 units/h =7 mL/h. NEVER use cloudy NPH IV
insulin-dka.maxDose: No universal fixed hourly ceiling; inadequate ketone fall needs line/pump and dose reassessment. Potassium <3.5 mmol/L requires urgent senior-led replacement and insulin review
monitoring: Hourly glucose and blood ketones; frequent VBG, potassium and electrolytes; target ketone fall ≥0.5 mmol/L/h
Add 10% glucose at 125 mL/h when glucose <14 mmol/L; euglycaemic pregnancy DKA may require glucose from the start
Continue usual long-acting basal insulin unless specialist contraindication; overlap IV insulin for 30–60 min after the appropriate subcutaneous meal dose during transition
contraindications: Severe hypokalaemia, shock, renal/cardiac disease require immediate specialist adaptation; never prescribe insulin without a fluid/potassium plan

norepinephrine-shock.indication: Persistent shock while fluid responsiveness/source control are addressed; first-line vasopressor in maternal septic shock
norepinephrine-shock.dose: Start 0.1 microgram/kg/min of NOREPINEPHRINE TARTRATE; increase by 0.05 microgram/kg/min as required
norepinephrine-shock.route: IV infusion pump through a suitable monitored large vein
norepinephrine-shock.frequency: Continuous infusion; MSF reassessment/titration every 10 min initially
norepinephrine-shock.duration: Until perfusion and BP recover; taper gradually, do not stop abruptly
norepinephrine-shock.preparation: For the cited stock 8 mg TARTRATE/4 mL (=4 mg BASE/4 mL): 2 mL contains 4 mg tartrate. Add 38 mL compatible fluid for FINAL 40 mL =100 micrograms TARTRATE/mL. Rate = dose × kg ×60 ÷100 mL/h; at 70 kg and 0.1, rate=4.2 mL/h
norepinephrine-shock.maxDose: MSF peripheral protocol ceiling 1 microgram/kg/min TARTRATE; persistent/escalating shock requires ICU and central/arterial access planning
monitoring: Continuous ECG, frequent BP (arterial when possible), perfusion and urine output; inspect peripheral site frequently for extravasation
Clearly label SALT versus BASE: this MSF tartrate dose is twice the numerical BASE dose; NEVER copy its pump rate into a base-labelled concentration
contraindications: Correct hypovolaemia in parallel; vasopressors do not replace haemorrhage control/blood replacement
Extravasation threatens tissue; use a dedicated monitored line, not an unobserved small distal cannula

heparin-pe.indication: Selected life-threatening PE, severe renal dysfunction or impending procedures when rapid reversibility is valuable
heparin-pe.dose: 80 units/kg IV loading, then 18 units/kg/hour; subsequent changes follow APTT/anti-Xa nomogram
heparin-pe.frequency: Continuous infusion after the initial loading dose
heparin-pe.duration: Until a definitive anticoagulation/reperfusion plan permits transition; duration individualised around bleeding and procedures
heparin-pe.preparation: Example: 25,000 units made up to FINAL 50 mL sodium chloride 0.9% =500 units/mL. Pump mL/h = prescribed units/h ÷500. Independently check vial units/mL, patient weight and label
heparin-pe.maxDose: No fixed cumulative ceiling; dose to APTT/anti-Xa with the approved nomogram. Omit/review bolus after thrombolysis or when bleeding risk requires
monitoring: Baseline CBC/platelets, coagulation and renal function; check APTT 6 h after starting and after dose changes
Bleeding, Hb/platelets, HIT risk and procedure/neuraxial timing
contraindications: Active major bleeding or HIT; recent surgery/neuraxial procedure requires a documented specialist risk plan

alteplase-pe.indication: Expert-led reperfusion decision for haemodynamically unstable massive PE; pregnancy/postpartum bleeding risks require simultaneous obstetric/critical-care input
alteplase-pe.dose: 100 mg over 2 hours (adult Activase-labelled PE regimen)
alteplase-pe.duration: 2-hour course followed by monitored anticoagulation planning; arrest dosing may follow a different resuscitation protocol
alteplase-pe.preparation: Reconstitute the specific 50/100 mg vial only with the supplied preservative-free sterile water to 1 mg/mL. Gently swirl, do not shake; use a dedicated line. This PE regimen differs from stroke dosing
alteplase-pe.maxDose: 100 mg for the cited adult PE regimen; check local product weight limits and do not borrow an arbitrary stroke bolus schedule
monitoring: Bleeding including genital/surgical/neuraxial sites, neurological status, BP, Hb and coagulation
Pause/restart heparin according to APTT and the thrombolysis plan; arrange blood products and procedural alternatives
contraindications: Major active bleeding, intracranial pathology/recent intracranial surgery and recent invasive procedures are major concerns
In immediately fatal PE, the multidisciplinary team weighs contraindications against the risk of death; do not apply this row to stable suspected PE

lorazepam-status.indication: Seizure lasting ≥5 min or recurrent seizures without recovery; also assess/treat eclampsia when possible
lorazepam-status.dose: 2 mg IV over 1 min; if not terminating, another 2 mg after 2–3 min (up to 4 mg); a repeat benzodiazepine dose at 10 min if still seizing under the GGC pathway
lorazepam-status.frequency: Initial staged dose; at most one repeat treatment before moving to second-line therapy
lorazepam-status.duration: Time-critical rescue; prepare airway/ventilation and second-line therapy concurrently
lorazepam-status.preparation: Use the actual IV lorazepam product; dilute according to its label. Prescribe in mg and verify mg/mL, including any dilution
lorazepam-status.maxDose: 4 mg initial treatment; count any benzodiazepine already given. Persistent status needs second-line loading and ICU, not endless benzodiazepines
monitoring: Airway, respiratory rate, SpO2, BP, ECG and glucose; assisted ventilation capability immediately available
contraindications: Respiratory depression is a major risk, especially after prior sedatives; do not mix several benzodiazepine schedules

levetiracetam-status.indication: Ongoing convulsive status after adequate first-line benzodiazepine treatment; non-eclamptic cause or seizures refractory to eclampsia care
levetiracetam-status.frequency: One loading dose with urgent reassessment
levetiracetam-status.duration: Emergency loading; ongoing maintenance is a separate neurology prescription
levetiracetam-status.preparation: 100 mg/mL concentrate: prescribed mg ÷100 =mL to withdraw. Dilute the dose in at least 100 mL compatible sodium chloride 0.9% and infuse over 15 min (Keppra product preparation); the 60 mg/kg, maximum 4500 mg status load is off-label GGC emergency guidance.
monitoring: Respiratory/circulatory monitoring, clinical seizure termination and EEG if consciousness fails to recover; renal function for subsequent maintenance
contraindications: Known levetiracetam allergy; persistent status needs anaesthesia/ICU and evaluation of cause

clindamycin-endometritis.indication: Postpartum endometritis, in combination with gentamicin when appropriate
clindamycin-endometritis.duration: Continue until clinical improvement and afebrile for 24–48 h in the cited NAG regimen; persistent fever needs source reassessment
clindamycin-endometritis.preparation: 150 mg/mL concentrate: 900 mg =6 mL; dilute in compatible IV fluid and infuse over at least 30 min (not IV push)
monitoring: Temperature, uterine tenderness, renal function/gentamicin levels for the partner drug; diarrhoea/C. difficile risk
contraindications: Clindamycin allergy; previous severe antibiotic-associated colitis requires assessment

calcium-hypocalcaemia.indication: Clinically important hypocalcaemia during major transfusion, guided by ionised calcium and physiology
calcium-hypocalcaemia.frequency: Initial dose followed by ionised-calcium/ECG reassessment; titrate further replacement to the monitored result
calcium-hypocalcaemia.duration: During the acute deficit and ongoing citrate exposure; stop/reduce when ionised calcium normalises
calcium-hypocalcaemia.preparation: 10% = 100 mg/mL; 10 mL contains 1 g calcium gluconate, NOT 1 g elemental calcium. Give over at least 5 min through a patent IV line; do not mix with other drugs
calcium-hypocalcaemia.maxDose: No fixed every-four-units schedule: reassess calcium and prescribe further doses explicitly
monitoring: Continuous ECG/heart rate; respiratory status, reflexes and injection site; serum calcium/magnesium where available
contraindications: Extravasation can cause tissue injury; take special care with digoxin
Do not confuse calcium gluconate with calcium chloride

adrenaline-refractory.indication: Persistent airway/breathing/circulation compromise after two appropriate IM doses; experienced critical-care/anaesthetic staff only
adrenaline-refractory.dose: Start 0.5–1 mL/kg/hour of the 10-microgram/mL solution according to severity, then titrate to response
adrenaline-refractory.duration: Until the reaction resolves and a supervised weaning/observation plan is established
adrenaline-refractory.preparation: Make 1 mg adrenaline up to FINAL 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9% =10 micrograms/mL. Use a dedicated labelled line and pump; do not piggyback where another infusion can cause an adrenaline bolus.
adrenaline-refractory.maxDose: No fixed universal rate ceiling; senior titration and invasive/continuous monitoring for refractory shock
monitoring: Continuous ECG, frequent/continuous BP, pulse, oxygenation and clinical response; inspect the IV line
Continue IM adrenaline every 5 min while arranging the expert infusion if compromise persists; do not delay initial IM treatment
contraindications: Do not start an unmonitored IV infusion or give IV boluses of the IM-strength solution
Tachyarrhythmia/marked hypertension needs immediate dose and line assessment
notes: At 70 kg, 0.5 mL/kg/hour =35 mL/hour =350 micrograms/hour (about 5.8 micrograms/min). The higher initial rate is chosen only by the experienced team.

enalapril-postpartum.indication: After birth only; NICE recommends enalapril with maternal renal-function and potassium monitoring
enalapril-postpartum.dose: Start 5 mg once daily; use a lower supervised initial dose if volume depleted or renally impaired; titrate to BP response
enalapril-postpartum.duration: Review BP and dose after birth; reduce/stop as hypertension resolves or continue for persistent hypertension after medical review
enalapril-postpartum.preparation: 5 mg tablet swallowed with water, with or without food. Correct volume depletion; check creatinine and potassium before starting
enalapril-postpartum.maxDose: 40 mg/day in the product label; usual maintenance 20 mg/day, not an automatic postpartum target
monitoring: BP, symptoms, creatinine/eGFR and potassium before and after initiation/dose changes; infant feeding, alertness and urine output if breastfeeding
contraindications: Pregnancy, prior ACE-inhibitor angioedema, significant hyperkalaemia; avoid starting in unresolved AKI or severe volume depletion
notes: NICE NG133 supplies the postpartum choice. Breastfeeding requires extra caution with premature/very young infants; use a suitable alternative when clinically indicated.
enalapril-postpartum.renalHepatic: Renal impairment requires a lower initial dose and adjustment from the product renal table, not the unadjusted 5 mg starter.

terbutaline-ecv.indication: Hospital external cephalic version after eligibility assessment, consent and baseline CTG
terbutaline-ecv.duration: One ECV attempt episode; not a maintenance preterm-labour regimen
terbutaline-ecv.preparation: 0.5 mg/mL ampoule: withdraw 0.5 mL =250 micrograms. This row is SC, not an interchangeable IV bolus
terbutaline-ecv.maxDose: 250 micrograms for the cited ECV regimen; no automatic repeat
monitoring: Maternal pulse/BP before treatment and pulse 5 minutes after; fetal assessment/CTG and immediate caesarean capability
contraindications: Cardiac disease; caution in diabetes and pre-eclampsia; ECV contraindications must be excluded
notes: Assess RhD status and provide indicated anti-D after ECV.

benzylpenicillin-gbs.indication: Intrapartum GBS prophylaxis when indicated, distinct from treatment of maternal sepsis
benzylpenicillin-gbs.dose: 3 g (5 million units) IV loading, then 1.5 g (2.5 million units) every 4 hours
benzylpenicillin-gbs.frequency: Load once, then every 4 hours until delivery
benzylpenicillin-gbs.duration: Intrapartum only; do not delay an indicated birth to complete four hours of antibiotics
benzylpenicillin-gbs.preparation: For the cited 1.2 g vial, dissolve each vial in at least 8 mL water for injections/0.9% saline for IV injection (powder displacement ~0.8 mL), or at least 20 mL for infusion. Account for final concentration when withdrawing partial vials. Give doses >1.2 g at least 1 minute per 300 mg: 3 g ≥10 min; 1.5 g ≥5 min
benzylpenicillin-gbs.maxDose: 3 g loading then 1.5 g every 4 hours; stop at birth. Do not confuse grams with million units.
monitoring: Allergy/anaphylaxis, renal function and timing of each dose; reassess fever/chorioamnionitis for a treatment combination
contraindications: Immediate severe penicillin/beta-lactam allergy requires a separately prescribed alternative based on allergy and susceptibility
notes: Do not confuse grams, milligrams and million units; ampicillin is a different regimen with 2 g loading then 1 g every 4 h.

levothyroxine-established.dose: At positive pregnancy test increase the weekly dose by about 25–30%, e.g. double the usual daily dose on two days each week; then titrate to TFTs
levothyroxine-established.frequency: Daily, with a clearly written seven-day dose schedule
levothyroxine-established.duration: Through pregnancy; make an individual postpartum dose plan and repeat TFTs about 6 weeks after birth
levothyroxine-established.preparation: Use the prescribed microgram-strength tablets consistently before breakfast; separate oral iron/calcium by 4–5 hours. Micrograms are not milligrams
levothyroxine-established.maxDose: No universal fixed maximum: titrate to pregnancy-specific TFTs; the initial 25–30% rise is not an instruction for repeated weekly increases
monitoring: TSH/FT4 every 4–6 weeks to 20 weeks and again at 28 weeks; target TSH <2.5 mIU/L with FT4 in the pregnancy reference range
contraindications: Untreated adrenal insufficiency requires assessment/treatment; avoid overreplacement in cardiac disease
notes: Pre-existing adequately treated disease generally returns to the preconception dose after birth according to the RCOG postpartum plan; reassess rather than automatically stopping permanent replacement.

levothyroxine-new.indication: RCOG: overt hypothyroidism or TSH >10 mIU/L; distinguish milder subclinical disease
levothyroxine-new.dose: Overt/severe disease: 1.6 micrograms/kg/day initial replacement. For selected subclinical disease with TSH above the gestational range but ≤10, consider 1.0–1.2 micrograms/kg/day after discussing benefit
levothyroxine-new.duration: Recheck TFTs after 4 weeks and titrate; postpartum continuation/withdrawal depends on the original diagnosis, dose and TFTs
levothyroxine-new.preparation: Calculate weight-based MICROGRAMS, prescribe an achievable tablet-strength schedule, take before breakfast and separate iron/calcium by 4–5 hours
levothyroxine-new.maxDose: Individualised TFT-guided dosing, not a fixed universal maximum
monitoring: TSH/FT4 after initiation and every 4–6 weeks during titration; reassess adherence and absorption before increasing
contraindications: Do not treat isolated low FT4 with normal TSH routinely; untreated adrenal insufficiency or cardiac disease requires specialist review
notes: The milder subclinical-treatment decision is separate from the clear indication to treat overt hypothyroidism.

ptu-graves.indication: Overt hyperthyroidism requiring antithyroid medication; preferred early-pregnancy option when appropriate
ptu-graves.dose: Product adult initial range 300–600 mg/day in divided doses until controlled; then usually 50–150 mg/day. In pregnancy use the lowest effective dose, individually selected from FT4 and severity, rather than automatically starting at the upper adult range
ptu-graves.frequency: Divide the prescribed daily dose, commonly every 8 hours
ptu-graves.duration: Titrate with specialist follow-up; if still needed beyond 20 weeks consider changing to carbimazole because of PTU hepatotoxicity
ptu-graves.preparation: 50 mg tablets; prescribe the exact mg per administration. Do not confuse the outpatient dose with the separate thyroid-storm loading regimen
ptu-graves.maxDose: 600 mg/day is the top of the cited adult starting range, not a routine pregnancy target or an instruction to escalate without endocrine review
monitoring: FT4/TSH every 2–4 weeks initially; urgent CBC for fever/sore throat; liver assessment for jaundice, dark urine or abdominal pain
contraindications: Previous PTU-associated hepatic injury/agranulocytosis; significant liver disease requires specialist choice
notes: RCOG: use the lowest dose maintaining FT4 in the upper half of its pregnancy range; do not titrate to a suppressed TSH alone. Do not use routine block-and-replace.
ptu-graves.renalHepatic: SmPC: GFR 10–50 mL/min use 75% dose; GFR <10 use 50%; reduce in hepatic disease with specialist review.

carbimazole-graves.indication: Specialist antithyroid option; pregnancy timing and PTU suitability determine selection
carbimazole-graves.dose: Adult product initial range 20–60 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses; maintenance usually 5–15 mg/day. Pregnancy requires the lowest effective dose. When switching, PTU 200 mg/day is approximately carbimazole 10 mg/day (20:1)
carbimazole-graves.frequency: Initially divided 2–3 times daily; maintenance may be once daily
carbimazole-graves.duration: Reassess TFTs within 2 weeks after a switch/dose change; continuation through pregnancy and after birth is individualised
carbimazole-graves.preparation: Use the stated tablet strength to deliver the exact mg; carbimazole and methimazole are not mg-for-mg equivalent
carbimazole-graves.maxDose: 60 mg/day is the adult label starting-range ceiling, not a routine pregnancy goal; thyroid-storm treatment is a separate regimen
monitoring: FT4/TSH, fever/sore-throat agranulocytosis warning, liver symptoms; fetal/neonatal surveillance when indicated
contraindications: Previous carbimazole/thiamazole-associated pancreatitis, serious marrow or liver disorder; first-trimester embryopathy risk requires specialist counselling
notes: RCOG advises considering PTU→carbimazole if antithyroid treatment is still needed beyond 20 weeks, rather than an automatic switch at the end of trimester 1. Routine block-and-replace is not recommended.

ptu-storm.indication: ICU/endocrine-led treatment of storm from increased hormone synthesis; assess pregnancy stage and hepatic function
ptu-storm.dose: 500–1000 mg loading, then 250 mg every 4 hours
ptu-storm.route: Oral or NG through a protected airway
ptu-storm.duration: Acute high-dose treatment only; reduce promptly as the patient stabilises, with an explicit endocrine maintenance plan
ptu-storm.preparation: 50 mg tablets: loading 10–20 tablets, maintenance 5 tablets per dose; pharmacy-assisted NG preparation if needed. Record administration before starting iodine
ptu-storm.maxDose: One initial load; 1500 mg/day maintenance at 250 mg every 4 h. No repeated loading without specialist reassessment
monitoring: Continuous cardiac/haemodynamic monitoring, temperature, mental state, glucose, FT4/FT3 and liver function; treat the precipitant
contraindications: Significant hepatic dysfunction/previous PTU liver injury favours an alternative thionamide with endocrine/hepatology input; destructive thyroiditis needs a different strategy
notes: 2026 joint statement: no proven mortality advantage over methimazole/carbimazole; drug selection must consider hepatic injury and pregnancy.
