propranolol-storm.indication: Adrenergic control only in haemodynamically stable patients without significant ventricular dysfunction
propranolol-storm.dose: The consensus lists 60–80 mg every 4 hours; assess cardiac function first and consider a lower initial dose because beta-blockade can precipitate collapse
propranolol-storm.route: Oral or NG with protected airway
propranolol-storm.frequency: Every 4 hours with reassessment before doses
propranolol-storm.duration: Only while required for acute thyrotoxicosis; taper/change as control improves
propranolol-storm.preparation: Immediate-release tablets, with exact mg prescribed; do not substitute sustained-release tablets or give this as an IV dose
propranolol-storm.maxDose: Listed oral schedule totals 360–480 mg/day; this is a specialist ICU regimen, not a routine pregnancy symptom-treatment dose
monitoring: Continuous ECG/BP/perfusion assessment, heart failure and bronchospasm; consider echocardiography before beta-blockade
contraindications: Shock, decompensated cardiac failure, significant bradycardia/heart block or asthma; short-acting titratable alternatives need critical-care supervision
notes: The 2026 statement emphasises individualisation and the possibility of cardiovascular collapse after beta-blockade.

hydrocortisone-storm.indication: Glucocorticoid component of ICU storm treatment
hydrocortisone-storm.dose: 100 mg IV loading, then 50 mg every 6 hours
hydrocortisone-storm.duration: Stop/review when stable if no accompanying adrenal insufficiency; the ongoing plan depends on cause and duration
hydrocortisone-storm.preparation: For the cited 100 mg powder vial add up to 2 mL sterile water for injections; if prepared with 2 mL, concentration is approximately 50 mg/mL: 100 mg=2 mL, 50 mg=1 mL. Give slowly over at least 1 minute and verify the actual product
hydrocortisone-storm.maxDose: 2026 joint-statement schedule: 100 mg load plus 200 mg/day maintenance, not a blended older 300 mg loading schedule
monitoring: Glucose, electrolytes, BP, infection and clinical recovery; reassess ongoing adrenal-support need
contraindications: Life-saving short-course use needs risk assessment rather than delaying treatment; review systemic fungal infection or known steroid hypersensitivity
notes: Preparation cross-checked against the Panpharma 100 mg powder product information; solution ampoules have different concentrations.

iodide-storm.drug: Potassium iodide — SSKI in thyroid storm
iodide-storm.indication: Short-course endocrine/ICU therapy after thionamide in hormone-synthesis-driven storm
iodide-storm.dose: SSKI 5 drops every 6 hours, starting at least 1 hour AFTER the antithyroid drug
iodide-storm.duration: Stop once stabilised/hormone levels controlled; prolonged iodine exposure in pregnancy can affect the fetal thyroid
iodide-storm.preparation: Use the pharmacy-verified SATURATED potassium iodide solution (SSKI, 1 g/mL), its calibrated dispenser and prescribed drop volume; dilute in milk/juice before oral/NG administration. Lugol solution is a different formulation and has a different drop prescription
iodide-storm.maxDose: 5 calibrated drops per dose in this regimen; never substitute an arbitrary dropper, radioactive-emergency tablets or Lugol drops
monitoring: Clinical recovery, FT4/FT3, hypersensitivity and pregnancy/neonatal thyroid planning
contraindications: Do not give before the thionamide; destructive/factitious thyrotoxicosis is not an indication for this synthesis-blocking sequence
notes: Product concentration confirmed against SSKI prescribing information. Do not prolong iodine in pregnancy without specialist review.

iron-oral-treatment.drug: Oral iron — treatment of pregnancy IDA
iron-oral-treatment.indication: Confirmed iron deficiency with anaemia; exclude haemoglobinopathy/other causes and assess urgency
iron-oral-treatment.dose: 120 mg ELEMENTAL iron per day (WHO treatment dose), with 400 micrograms folic acid daily
iron-oral-treatment.frequency: Daily; divide the elemental-iron dose if needed for tolerability
iron-oral-treatment.duration: Until Hb normalises, then return to the preventive antenatal dose; continue the documented postnatal/repletion plan rather than stopping after an arbitrary pack
iron-oral-treatment.preparation: Count ELEMENTAL iron, not total salt mass. A tablet containing 60 mg elemental iron gives 120 mg with two tablets; check combined-tablet folate content separately. Separate from calcium by several hours and from levothyroxine by 4–5 hours
iron-oral-treatment.maxDose: 120 mg/day elemental iron in this WHO treatment regimen; extra OTC iron can duplicate treatment
monitoring: Hb response after 2–4 weeks, adherence, GI effects and evidence of iron deficiency; investigate non-response and consider IV replacement when indicated
contraindications: Iron overload or non-iron-deficiency anaemia; oral treatment is inadequate as sole treatment of unstable major bleeding
notes: Daily WHO treatment and prevention doses are different. Alternate-day strategies need an explicit alternative prescription and response review.

iron-folate-prevention.indication: Routine pregnancy supplementation, particularly high-anaemia-burden settings
iron-folate-prevention.dose: 60 mg ELEMENTAL iron +400 micrograms (0.4 mg) folic acid
iron-folate-prevention.duration: Throughout pregnancy, beginning as early as possible; document any national postpartum continuation separately
iron-folate-prevention.preparation: Choose a product labelled with these elemental-iron/folate amounts; no dilution. Check other prenatal supplements to avoid duplication; separate calcium and levothyroxine
iron-folate-prevention.maxDose: WHO preventive range is 30–60 mg elemental iron/day; this card selects 60 mg. Do not treat established IDA with the preventive dose alone
monitoring: Hb/anaemia screening, tolerance, adherence and additional risk of folate/B12 deficiency
contraindications: Known iron overload; assess microcytosis/non-response rather than repeatedly escalating iron blindly
notes: Start folic acid before conception where possible. High-risk neural-tube-defect prevention is a separate higher-dose folate prescription.

calcium-antenatal.indication: WHO prevention of pre-eclampsia in populations with low dietary calcium intake
calcium-antenatal.dose: 1.5–2 g ELEMENTAL calcium per day; a practical 1.5 g schedule is 500 mg three times daily
calcium-antenatal.frequency: Three divided doses, preferably with meals
calcium-antenatal.duration: During pregnancy; starting time and postpartum continuation should be documented for the national programme used
calcium-antenatal.preparation: Read elemental calcium on the label: salt weight is not elemental calcium. Use 500 mg elemental-calcium tablets for the example schedule; separate iron by several hours and levothyroxine by 4–5 hours
calcium-antenatal.maxDose: 2 g/day supplemental elemental calcium in this WHO regimen; count all supplements and assess renal/stone risk
monitoring: Dietary intake, adherence, renal disease and duplicate calcium/vitamin-D products
contraindications: Hypercalcaemia; renal impairment or recurrent calcium stones require individual assessment
notes: WHO notes that evidence does not establish one optimal start time; supplementation may begin at the first antenatal contact.

promethazine-hg.indication: First-line antihistamine option in RCOG HG guidance
promethazine-hg.frequency: Every 4–8 hours as prescribed; use the lowest effective frequency
promethazine-hg.duration: Review daily during acute illness; reduce/stop as symptoms and oral intake improve
promethazine-hg.preparation: Use oral tablets/liquid of a verified strength; 12.5 mg requires a suitable product rather than assuming every tablet can be split
promethazine-hg.maxDose: The listed 25 mg every 4 h schedule totals 150 mg/day; this is a regimen bound, not a target, and sedation may require much less
monitoring: Sedation, anticholinergic effects, oral intake and interactions with other sedatives/QT-prolonging drugs
contraindications: Significant CNS/respiratory depression; avoid alcohol and additive sedation; do not drive when drowsy
notes: This row is ORAL. Injectable promethazine is not interchangeable and has separate tissue-injury/administration precautions.

metoclopramide-hg.indication: RCOG second-line antiemetic after assessing hydration and prior treatments
metoclopramide-hg.frequency: Every 8 hours; leave at least 6 hours between any two doses even if vomiting
metoclopramide-hg.duration: At most 5 days in the product safety restriction; reassess rather than issuing an indefinite repeat
metoclopramide-hg.preparation: 5 or 10 mg oral formulation; check strength. Do not automatically repeat a vomited dose before the minimum interval
monitoring: Acute dystonia/akathisia, drowsiness, response, hydration and renal function; stop if neurological adverse effects occur
contraindications: GI obstruction/perforation/bleeding, epilepsy, Parkinson disease, phaeochromocytoma, prior tardive dyskinesia; avoid with levodopa
notes: RCOG places this after first-line options because of extrapyramidal reactions.
metoclopramide-hg.renalHepatic: CrCl 15–60: reduce daily dose by 50%; ≤15: reduce by 75%; severe hepatic impairment: reduce by 50%.

ursodeoxycholic-icp.indication: Maternal itching in confirmed intrahepatic cholestasis; not a substitute for bile-acid-based birth planning
ursodeoxycholic-icp.dose: Start 10–15 mg/kg/day in 2–3 divided doses; adjust to symptoms with specialist review
ursodeoxycholic-icp.duration: Until birth with symptom/liver-test review; confirm postnatal resolution
ursodeoxycholic-icp.preparation: Prescribe mg from maternal weight and available capsule/tablet strength. Example 60 kg at 10 mg/kg/day =600 mg/day, e.g. 300 mg twice daily if that formulation is available
ursodeoxycholic-icp.maxDose: SMFM permits escalation up to 21 mg/kg/day for persistent symptoms; do not increase indefinitely
monitoring: Itch, bile acids/LFTs and treatment tolerance; repeat postnatal liver tests/bile acids at about 6 weeks
contraindications: Exclude other liver disease/obstruction; urgent assessment for jaundice/coagulopathy or alternative diagnoses
notes: SMFM/ACOG-endorsed guidance supplies the dose. RCOG counselling: symptom benefit is limited and UDCA does not prevent stillbirth.

acyclovir-initial.duration: 7–10 days; extend if healing remains incomplete after 10 days
acyclovir-initial.preparation: 400 mg tablet (or two 200 mg tablets); maintain hydration and check renal function; not an IV prescription
acyclovir-initial.maxDose: 1200 mg/day for this schedule; adjust with renal impairment
monitoring: Lesion/symptom response, renal function and delivery/neonatal-risk assessment
contraindications: Acyclovir/valacyclovir allergy; severe/disseminated/CNS infection needs hospital IV treatment instead
notes: Suppression reduces recurrence but does not eliminate neonatal transmission; first acquisition near birth needs specialist obstetric/neonatal planning.

acyclovir-pregnancy-suppression.indication: Recurrent genital herpes in pregnancy: CDC suppression from 36 weeks
acyclovir-pregnancy-suppression.duration: From 36 weeks until birth; reassess delivery route if lesions/prodrome occur
acyclovir-pregnancy-suppression.preparation: 400 mg tablet (or two 200 mg tablets); maintain hydration and check renal function; not an IV prescription
acyclovir-pregnancy-suppression.maxDose: 1200 mg/day for this schedule; adjust with renal impairment
monitoring: Lesion/symptom response, renal function and delivery/neonatal-risk assessment
contraindications: Acyclovir/valacyclovir allergy; severe/disseminated/CNS infection needs hospital IV treatment instead
notes: Suppression reduces recurrence but does not eliminate neonatal transmission; first acquisition near birth needs specialist obstetric/neonatal planning.

mirena-hmb.indication: Heavy menstrual bleeding after evaluating uterine/cervical/endometrial pathology
mirena-hmb.frequency: One insertion by a trained clinician
mirena-hmb.duration: 5 years for HMB, then reassess symptoms; replace/remove if bleeding returns
mirena-hmb.preparation: Sterile, single-use Mirena system and inserter; aseptic insertion after assessment of uterine position/cavity and infection/pregnancy exclusion. Record insertion date and indication-specific removal date
mirena-hmb.maxDose: One device; contraception duration (8 years) must not be applied to HRT endometrial protection (4 years in the UK label)
monitoring: Bleeding/pain, expulsion/perforation symptoms, thread/insertion follow-up and pregnancy symptoms; investigate persistent/new abnormal bleeding
contraindications: Pregnancy, active pelvic/cervical infection, unexplained bleeding until assessed, uterine cavity distortion, current hormone-dependent tumour or acute severe liver disease
notes: 52 mg systems/indications are not interchangeable with lower-dose IUS products. HMB symptom recurrence requires reassessment before assuming device failure.

mirena-contraception.indication: Contraception after pregnancy exclusion and eligibility assessment
mirena-contraception.frequency: One insertion by a trained clinician
mirena-contraception.duration: Up to 8 years for contraception with this specific Mirena 52 mg product
mirena-contraception.preparation: Sterile, single-use Mirena system and inserter; aseptic insertion after assessment of uterine position/cavity and infection/pregnancy exclusion. Record insertion date and indication-specific removal date
mirena-contraception.maxDose: One device; contraception duration (8 years) must not be applied to HRT endometrial protection (4 years in the UK label)
monitoring: Bleeding/pain, expulsion/perforation symptoms, thread/insertion follow-up and pregnancy symptoms; investigate persistent/new abnormal bleeding
contraindications: Pregnancy, active pelvic/cervical infection, unexplained bleeding until assessed, uterine cavity distortion, current hormone-dependent tumour or acute severe liver disease
notes: 52 mg systems/indications are not interchangeable with lower-dose IUS products. HMB symptom recurrence requires reassessment before assuming device failure.

letrozole-ovulation.indication: Anovulatory PCOS infertility after assessment of pregnancy, tubal/semen factors and counselling about off-label use
letrozole-ovulation.frequency: Once daily for 5 consecutive days per prescribed cycle
letrozole-ovulation.duration: Initial monitored cycle, with review of ovulation/response before changing dose or repeating a course
letrozole-ovulation.preparation: One 2.5 mg tablet daily; day 1 is the first day of fresh menstrual bleeding. Exclude pregnancy before another cycle if no period
letrozole-ovulation.maxDose: 2.5 mg/day in this named NHS starting regimen; dose escalation requires a new fertility prescription, not automatic self-escalation
monitoring: Ovulation assessment, cycle/pregnancy outcome and ultrasound monitoring where indicated; discuss multiple-pregnancy risk
contraindications: Possible/existing pregnancy, breastfeeding; hepatic impairment needs specialist assessment
notes: PCOS 2023 guidance supports letrozole first line for anovulatory infertility without other infertility factors. Cycle-day schedules vary by clinic; follow one complete prescribed schedule.

metformin-pcos.indication: Metabolic features of PCOS, particularly adults with BMI ≥25; not an interchangeable GDM regimen
metformin-pcos.dose: Start 500 mg/day with food; increase by 500 mg every 1–2 weeks if tolerated toward the individually required dose
metformin-pcos.frequency: Once daily initially, then divided with meals; extended-release requires its own product instructions
metformin-pcos.duration: Continue while metabolic benefit outweighs adverse effects; review the indication when pregnancy occurs
metformin-pcos.preparation: Use 500 mg immediate-release tablets for this example; slow titration reduces GI effects
metformin-pcos.maxDose: Suggested PCOS guideline maximum 2.5 g/day in adults and 2 g/day in adolescents, subject to the lower licensed product/renal limit
monitoring: Metabolic response, renal function, GI tolerance and B12 if risk factors/long-term therapy
contraindications: eGFR <30, metabolic acidosis, hypoxia or major dehydration; withhold during serious acute illness
notes: Lifestyle treatment remains foundational. Letrozole is the separate first-line ovulation-induction option.

coc-ee-lng.indication: Eligible nonpregnant patient seeking contraception or PCOS cycle control after BP/VTE/migraine assessment
coc-ee-lng.dose: One active tablet containing ethinylestradiol 30 micrograms +levonorgestrel 150 micrograms daily for 21 days, followed by the 7 inactive tablets in the cited 28-day pack
coc-ee-lng.frequency: One tablet at the same time daily, including inactive tablets; start the next pack immediately after day 28
coc-ee-lng.duration: Ongoing while eligible, with periodic BP/risk review; stop and assess new contraindications
coc-ee-lng.preparation: Check the pack has 21 active +7 inactive tablets of the stated formulation. Other pill formulations and extended regimens need their own schedule
coc-ee-lng.maxDose: One scheduled tablet/day; missed-pill/vomiting instructions are a separate decision pathway, not a reason for indefinite extra dosing
monitoring: BP, adherence, bleeding, new migraine aura or VTE symptoms; review interacting medicines
contraindications: Migraine with aura, active/prior VTE or major thrombotic risk, uncontrolled hypertension, smoking ≥35 years, current breast cancer or severe liver disease; postpartum eligibility is time/breastfeeding dependent
notes: If starting >5 days after menstrual bleeding begins, use backup for 7 days. This formulation is an example; PCOS guidance does not establish one universally preferred progestogen.

estradiol-hrt.indication: Menopausal symptoms after individual assessment; intact uterus also needs adequate progestogen
estradiol-hrt.dose: One patch releasing 50 micrograms per 24 hours
estradiol-hrt.duration: Use the lowest effective dose with regular benefit/risk review; review new bleeding promptly
estradiol-hrt.preparation: Apply to clean dry intact abdominal skin, never the breasts; rotate sites, avoid waistline and do not cut the patch. Remove the old patch when replacing
estradiol-hrt.maxDose: This starting example is 50 micrograms/24 h; higher strengths require reassessment and proportionate progestogen
monitoring: Symptom response, bleeding, BP and changing breast/VTE/liver risk
contraindications: Unexplained genital bleeding, known/suspected oestrogen-dependent cancer, active/prior VTE, arterial thrombosis or active liver disease; pregnancy/breastfeeding
notes: The dose is a RELEASE RATE per 24 hours; it does not mean applying a new patch every day. HRT is not contraception.

progesterone-hrt-sequential.indication: Endometrial protection with standard-dose systemic oestrogen in a patient with a uterus
progesterone-hrt-sequential.dose: 200 mg at bedtime for 12–14 days in each 28-day/monthly cycle
progesterone-hrt-sequential.frequency: Nightly on the prescribed 12–14 days each cycle
progesterone-hrt-sequential.duration: For as long as systemic oestrogen is used with an intact uterus; review bleeding and increase protection if oestrogen dose increases
progesterone-hrt-sequential.preparation: Use oral micronised-progesterone capsules: 200 mg =two 100 mg capsules where that is the available strength. Do not substitute an unverified compounded or vaginal product
progesterone-hrt-sequential.maxDose: This standard-dose-oestrogen schedule is 200 mg cyclic OR 100 mg daily, not both; high-dose oestrogen needs a revised progestogen prescription
monitoring: Sedation, adherence to the full monthly course and new/persistent unscheduled bleeding
contraindications: Unexplained bleeding, hormone-dependent malignancy or serious liver disease require assessment; check the actual capsule excipients/allergies
notes: Choose sequential or continuous treatment according to menopausal phase and clinical assessment; never omit protection because a patch is used.

progesterone-hrt-continuous.indication: Endometrial protection with standard-dose systemic oestrogen in a patient with a uterus
progesterone-hrt-continuous.duration: For as long as systemic oestrogen is used with an intact uterus; review bleeding and increase protection if oestrogen dose increases
progesterone-hrt-continuous.preparation: Use oral micronised-progesterone capsules: 200 mg =two 100 mg capsules where that is the available strength. Do not substitute an unverified compounded or vaginal product
progesterone-hrt-continuous.maxDose: This standard-dose-oestrogen schedule is 200 mg cyclic OR 100 mg daily, not both; high-dose oestrogen needs a revised progestogen prescription
monitoring: Sedation, adherence to the full monthly course and new/persistent unscheduled bleeding
contraindications: Unexplained bleeding, hormone-dependent malignancy or serious liver disease require assessment; check the actual capsule excipients/allergies
notes: Choose sequential or continuous treatment according to menopausal phase and clinical assessment; never omit protection because a patch is used.

anti-d-routine.indication: Non-sensitised RhD-negative pregnancy with an indication for routine antenatal prophylaxis
anti-d-routine.route: IM or IV for this Rhophylac product only
anti-d-routine.duration: One routine antenatal dose; sensitising events and birth are assessed separately
anti-d-routine.preparation: Ready-to-use prefilled syringe 300 micrograms/2 mL (1500 IU/2 mL); bring to room temperature and give slowly. Verify product, RhD status and antibody screen; do not confuse with newborn vitamin K
anti-d-routine.maxDose: One 300-microgram syringe covers approximately 15 mL fetal RhD-positive red cells; additional dose depends on measured FMH, not an arbitrary universal ceiling
monitoring: Identity/product checks, prior sensitisation, allergic reactions and FMH assessment; observe after administration
contraindications: RhD-positive mother or established immune anti-D: prophylaxis is not treatment; IM route unsuitable with severe thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy
notes: Give to the mother, not the infant. Early-pregnancy losses have separate gestation/management criteria; do not apply the routine 28-week row to every miscarriage.

anti-d-postpartum.indication: Non-sensitised RhD-negative mother after an RhD-positive birth
anti-d-postpartum.dose: 300 micrograms (1500 IU); increase if testing shows a larger fetomaternal haemorrhage
anti-d-postpartum.route: IM or IV for this Rhophylac product only
anti-d-postpartum.frequency: Once as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours of birth
anti-d-postpartum.duration: Postnatal episode; if >72 hours have elapsed, do not withhold—give as soon as possible and obtain specialist advice
anti-d-postpartum.preparation: Ready-to-use prefilled syringe 300 micrograms/2 mL (1500 IU/2 mL); bring to room temperature and give slowly. Verify product, RhD status and antibody screen; do not confuse with newborn vitamin K
anti-d-postpartum.maxDose: One 300-microgram syringe covers approximately 15 mL fetal RhD-positive red cells; additional dose depends on measured FMH, not an arbitrary universal ceiling
monitoring: Identity/product checks, prior sensitisation, allergic reactions and FMH assessment; observe after administration
contraindications: RhD-positive mother or established immune anti-D: prophylaxis is not treatment; IM route unsuitable with severe thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy
notes: Give to the mother, not the infant. Early-pregnancy losses have separate gestation/management criteria; do not apply the routine 28-week row to every miscarriage.

nitrofurantoin-lower.dose: 100 mg modified release twice daily; if unavailable, 50 mg immediate release four times daily
nitrofurantoin-lower.preparation: Take with food using the specified modified-release capsule or immediate-release product; do not exchange frequency between formulations
nitrofurantoin-lower.maxDose: 200 mg/day in either cited pregnancy lower-UTI regimen
monitoring: Symptoms, culture/susceptibility, renal function and clinical response by 48 hours; stop/review pulmonary or hepatic symptoms
contraindications: Avoid at term, in G6PD deficiency and significant renal impairment; fever/loin pain or sepsis requires an upper-UTI pathway
notes: NICE routine eligibility is eGFR ≥45 mL/min; eGFR 30–44 use is exceptional and needs a specific resistance/benefit-risk assessment.

cefalexin-lower.indication: NICE second-choice lower-UTI option when suitable for culture results/allergy history
cefalexin-lower.preparation: 500 mg capsule/tablet; swallow with water. If a suspension is used, verify its concentration and measure the prescribed mg
cefalexin-lower.maxDose: 1000 mg/day in this uncomplicated lower-UTI regimen; other infections have different schedules
monitoring: Culture/susceptibility, response within 48 hours, allergy, diarrhoea and renal function
contraindications: Cephalosporin allergy; assess severe immediate beta-lactam allergy. Systemic/upper-UTI features need a different regimen
notes: Dose adjustment is required with renal impairment. This is not the pyelonephritis step-down prescription for every organism.

benzathine-early.indication: Primary, secondary or early latent syphilis after staging
benzathine-early.frequency: One initial dose; in pregnancy CDC permits an additional 2.4-million-unit dose one week later
benzathine-early.duration: Initial episode; document any indicated extra dose and follow-up
benzathine-early.preparation: Use a product labelled penicillin G BENZATHINE alone, e.g. the full prefilled Bicillin L-A syringe labelled 2.4 million units (nominal 4 mL presentation); no dilution. Powder products require their own manufacturer reconstitution, and overfill means the prefilled presentation is not a universal units/mL recipe
benzathine-early.maxDose: 2.4 million units per dose; do not substitute benzathine for neurosyphilis therapy
monitoring: Allergy/anaphylaxis readiness; injection-site/vascular safety; warn about Jarisch–Herxheimer reaction and fetal symptoms; stage-appropriate maternal titres and neonatal planning
contraindications: Never IV, intra-arterial or into/near a nerve/vessel; pregnancy with true penicillin allergy requires desensitisation for effective fetal treatment
notes: Confirm the exact penicillin salt/product. Bicillin L-A is not Bicillin C-R and is not aqueous crystalline penicillin.

benzathine-late.indication: Late latent syphilis or unknown duration without neurosyphilis
benzathine-late.duration: Three-weekly-dose course; >9 days between doses in pregnancy requires restarting the full course
benzathine-late.preparation: Use a product labelled penicillin G BENZATHINE alone, e.g. the full prefilled Bicillin L-A syringe labelled 2.4 million units (nominal 4 mL presentation); no dilution. Powder products require their own manufacturer reconstitution, and overfill means the prefilled presentation is not a universal units/mL recipe
benzathine-late.maxDose: 7.2 million units total across three correctly timed doses
monitoring: Allergy/anaphylaxis readiness; injection-site/vascular safety; warn about Jarisch–Herxheimer reaction and fetal symptoms; stage-appropriate maternal titres and neonatal planning
contraindications: Never IV, intra-arterial or into/near a nerve/vessel; pregnancy with true penicillin allergy requires desensitisation for effective fetal treatment
notes: Confirm the exact penicillin salt/product. Bicillin L-A is not Bicillin C-R and is not aqueous crystalline penicillin.

benzyl-neurosyphilis.indication: Adult neurosyphilis, ocular or otosyphilis with specialist evaluation
benzyl-neurosyphilis.dose: 4 million units (2.4 g) IV every 4 hours; this selects the upper end of the CDC 18–24-million-unit/day range
benzyl-neurosyphilis.duration: 10–14 days; additional stage-dependent benzathine treatment may be considered after completion
benzyl-neurosyphilis.preparation: For the cited 1.2 g (2-million-unit) sodium vials, use two vials per 2.4 g dose. Dissolve each in at least 8 mL water for injections/0.9% saline and give the complete dose slowly over at least 8 minutes (label: ≥1 minute per 300 mg). For infusion, reconstitute each vial in at least 20 mL compatible fluid. Verify the local product and account for sodium/fluid load
benzyl-neurosyphilis.maxDose: 24 million units/day in this selected schedule; reduce/adjust for significant renal impairment
monitoring: Clinical/neurological and ophthalmic/otic assessment, renal function, electrolytes, allergy and treatment completion
contraindications: Benzathine IM penicillin does not treat neurosyphilis adequately; severe allergy in pregnancy requires desensitisation and specialist care
notes: Dose from CDC; preparation from the registered benzylpenicillin sodium SmPC. Potassium and sodium formulations have different electrolyte loads.

clindamycin-bv.indication: Symptomatic bacterial vaginosis when an oral alternative is appropriate
clindamycin-bv.preparation: 300 mg capsule or two 150 mg capsules per dose; swallow with a full glass of water
clindamycin-bv.maxDose: 600 mg/day in this BV regimen, separate from 900 mg IV emergency dosing
monitoring: Symptom response, intolerance and severe/persistent diarrhoea suggestive of C. difficile
contraindications: Clindamycin/lincomycin allergy; previous antibiotic-associated colitis needs careful assessment
notes: Do not shorten this CDC pregnancy BV course to five days.

clotrimazole-pregnancy.indication: Symptomatic confirmed/suspected vulvovaginal candidiasis; reconsider other diagnoses with persistent symptoms
clotrimazole-pregnancy.dose: 5 g of 1% vaginal cream (50 mg clotrimazole)
clotrimazole-pregnancy.preparation: Use a product intended for VAGINAL use with a measured 5 g dose; 1% cream is not interchangeable with a 2% three-day course or external vulval cream. Discuss insertion technique in pregnancy using the actual product instructions
clotrimazole-pregnancy.maxDose: One 5 g application/day for this regimen; persistent/recurrent disease needs assessment rather than repeated blind treatment
monitoring: Symptom response, local irritation and recurrence; culture/speciation when complicated or refractory
contraindications: Clotrimazole allergy; avoid oral fluconazole during pregnancy and do not use vaginal boric acid as a routine pregnancy alternative
notes: CDC recommends topical azoles for seven days during pregnancy. Check product effects on latex contraception.

dinoprostone-iol.indication: Hospital induction in an eligible unscarred uterus after cervical/fetal assessment; alternative to other ripening medicines
dinoprostone-iol.dose: 3 mg vaginally; if labour is not established, one further 3 mg tablet after 6–8 hours
dinoprostone-iol.frequency: Initial dose, then at most ONE repeat at 6–8 hours if eligible
dinoprostone-iol.duration: One induction course, with reassessment after the maximum; stop further dosing for labour/hyperstimulation or fetal concern
dinoprostone-iol.preparation: Use the specific Prostin E2 3 mg VAGINAL TABLET, inserted high in the posterior fornix by trained staff. Gel and controlled-release inserts have different strengths/schedules
dinoprostone-iol.maxDose: 6 mg total; wait at least 6 hours after dinoprostone before oxytocin
monitoring: Uterine activity and fetal heart rate, maternal observations, hypertonus/tachysystole and signs of rupture; emergency obstetric cover
contraindications: Previous caesarean/major uterine surgery, disproportion, malpresentation, suspected fetal distress, placenta praevia/unexplained bleeding or contraindication to labour
notes: Do not give together with misoprostol or oxytocin as a stacked ripening regimen; asthma and major cardiac/renal/hepatic disease require assessment.

paracetamol-acute-pain.indication: Short-term maternal postoperative/postpartum pain or other mild pain after assessment; adult ≥50 kg
paracetamol-acute-pain.frequency: Every 6–8 hours when needed; maximum 4 doses in 24 hours
paracetamol-acute-pain.duration: According to clinical response: reduce/stop as pain improves. Record the prescribed supply and review date; persistent or increasing pain needs reassessment rather than an automatic repeat course.
paracetamol-acute-pain.preparation: Check tablet strength: two 500 mg tablets = 1 g. Count paracetamol in every combination/OTC product towards the total; this is not an IV preparation.
paracetamol-acute-pain.maxDose: 4 g in 24 hours for the stated adult population. Lower weight, hepatic impairment or other risk factors require an individual reduced prescription; do not automatically use this maximum.
monitoring: Pain and functional recovery; investigate increasing pain, fever or other warning symptoms.
Check all prescribed/OTC paracetamol, weight and hepatic risk; suspected excess dosing requires urgent assessment.
contraindications: Paracetamol allergy; avoid duplicate paracetamol-containing products.
Hepatic impairment needs caution and a clinician-adjusted regimen. This adult ≥50 kg card is not a weight-based prescription for smaller adults or children.
notes: MSF oral monograph: no pregnancy or breastfeeding contraindication. The dose does not replace assessment of the cause of pain.

ibuprofen-postpartum-pain.indication: Short-term pain relief after birth or gynaecological surgery when NSAIDs are appropriate; not an antenatal regimen
ibuprofen-postpartum-pain.frequency: Every 8 hours when prescribed; reduce/stop as symptoms improve
ibuprofen-postpartum-pain.duration: Shortest course needed for recovery; MSF postoperative reference maximum 8 days. Record the actual stop/review date; ongoing or increasing pain needs clinical review.
ibuprofen-postpartum-pain.preparation: Check 200 mg or 400 mg tablet strength. Take with food; do not combine with another NSAID or duplicate OTC ibuprofen.
ibuprofen-postpartum-pain.maxDose: 1,200 mg in 24 hours in this pain regimen; do not import higher anti-inflammatory schedules into a discharge prescription.
monitoring: Pain response, hydration/urine output, GI pain or bleeding; review renal function when clinically indicated.
Check current bleeding, renal/hepatic function, allergy/asthma history, anticoagulants and interacting medicines before prescribing.
contraindications: NSAID allergy or NSAID-triggered asthma; active peptic ulcer/GI bleeding or a significant bleeding/coagulation problem.
Severe renal/hepatic impairment, severe heart failure, uncorrected dehydration/hypovolaemia or severe infection. Avoid in OHSS because of renal risk.
Avoid concurrent NSAIDs; anticoagulants, methotrexate, ACE inhibitors/diuretics and other interacting medicines require prescriber review. This card is for postpartum/nonpregnant care, not pregnancy.
notes: Short-term use is compatible with breastfeeding in the MSF reference. Do not prescribe while bleeding or renal contraindications remain unresolved.

iron-postpartum-treatment.drug: Oral iron and folic acid — postpartum anaemia treatment
iron-postpartum-treatment.indication: Diagnosed postpartum iron-deficiency anaemia after haemorrhage is controlled and outpatient oral treatment is suitable
iron-postpartum-treatment.dose: 120 mg ELEMENTAL iron plus 400 micrograms folic acid per day
iron-postpartum-treatment.frequency: Daily; tailor administration for tolerance without accidentally changing the prescribed total
iron-postpartum-treatment.duration: WHO postpartum anaemia treatment: until Hb normalises. Then document any continuing preventive/repletion course and review; the preventive 6–12-week recommendation is a different indication.
iron-postpartum-treatment.preparation: Use the product’s ELEMENTAL iron content, not salt weight: two tablets each containing 60 mg elemental iron provide 120 mg. Check the combined-tablet folate separately. Separate iron from calcium by several hours and levothyroxine by 4–5 hours.
iron-postpartum-treatment.maxDose: 120 mg/day elemental iron in this WHO treatment schedule; do not add duplicate antenatal/OTC iron or overlap oral and IV courses without an explicit plan.
monitoring: Arrange Hb response review after 2–4 weeks, tolerance and adherence; investigate non-response or ongoing bleeding and reassess the replacement route.
Review the cause of anaemia and any coexisting B12/folate deficiency or haemoglobinopathy.
contraindications: Iron overload or anaemia without iron deficiency; oral iron alone is inadequate for unstable bleeding or cardiovascular compromise.
notes: The WHO 2025 supportive-care recommendation supplies the postpartum dose/endpoint. Preparation and response monitoring reuse the checked oral-iron reference; breastfeeding is compatible with indicated maternal supplementation.
